rows.title_full: FIRST ANNIVERSARY OF THE CREATION OF \"SANSHA CITY\" BY CHINA TO ADMINISTER THE WEST PHLIPPINE SEA
rows.title_short: Chinese Claims On West Philippine Sea
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. BELLO (W.)
Rep. Bello pointed out that China established
Sansha City the previous year in order to oversee
and administer the West Philippine Sea and
adjacent waters and assert ownership over islands
and terrestrial features thereat based on a so-called nine-dash-line map. He said that the Philippines had advocated multilateral diplomacy to resolve the dispute with China and had been able to get the support of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) for peaceful dispute resolution and the United Nations, for international arbitration. He added that China had threatened force and had said that it only wanted bilateral talks to resolve the matter but that it had recently agreed to participate in talks to come up with a code of conduct to govern the behavior of different claimants.
Rep. Bello then stressed that the Philippines´
stand goes beyond protecting national interest as it would affect freedom of navigation in the world´s seas and oceans. After discussing the reasons behind China´s aggression, he also said that the country must not only counter Chinese hegemony but also United States (US) efforts to escalate its military presence in the region.
As the international community stands behind
the Philippine government´s efforts to defend its
interest in the West Philippine Sea, Rep. Bello
informed the Body that Filipinos will hold protest rallies in major cities all over the world the following day to condemn China´s aggression towards the Philippines and push for a diplomatic solution to the issue.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
Reps. Bello (W.) and Biazon discussed the status
of the Philippine Baseline Law and whether it is in compliance with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Rep. Biazon stated that any protest filed in relation to disputes in territorial water boundaries and exclusive economic zones among nations will have to be referred to the UNCLOS which provides for arbitration or bilateral agreement between the disputing countries. Rep. Bello pointed out that the Philippine government has submitted to the UNCLOS its claims to the West Philippine Sea in order to peacefully clarify the legitimacy of the other claimant-countries. In conclusion, both Members agreed that at the appropriate time, Congress should inquire into the
issue and formulate a national policy on the matter.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. TINIO
Rep. Tinio discussed with Rep. Bello (W.) the
organizations of Filipinos in the US, Europe,
Australia and the Philippines involved in the protests against the Chinese claim in the West Philippine Sea, particularly the US-Pinoy for Good Governance led by Ms. Loida Nicolas-Lewis, a prominent Filipino expatriate who actively supports US President Barack Obama and his Democratic Party. Their discussion then focused on the trip made by Rep. Bello with three other Members of the 15th Congress to the Kalayaan Group of Islands, which the former clarified was financed by Ms. Nicolas-Lewis´ group. Rep. Tinio expressed discomfort over the fact that said trip was funded by a person whose government has its own vested interest in the area.
(Continuation)
Rep. Bello (W.) clarified that whatever Ms.
Nicolas-Lewis´ views are with respect to the US
government in the West Philippine Sea, and that
insofar as the four Members who went to the Spratly Islands were concerned, they are all but united in supporting the interests of the country against the aggressive behavior of China, and that they do not support any US efforts to remilitarize the area.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Banal, Rep. Rufus B. Rodriguez discussed with Rep. Bello (W.) the West Philippine Sea conflict between the Philippines and China and the corresponding actions of the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) thereon, which included UN international arbitration.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
(Continuation)
Reps. Bello (W.) and Rodriguez discussed the
three major issues presented by the DFA to the
compulsory arbitral tribunal in Hamburg, Germany
that needed to be clarified with respect to China´s claim to the West Philippine Sea, to wit: 1) whether China´s claimed historic right to the so-called ninedash line has basis in the UNCLOS; 2) the classification of the Panatag or Scarborough Shoal and the Bajo de Masinloc; and 3) the character and status of the structures in the Panganiban or Mischief Reef. They also talked about the position of Akbayan that allowing American armed forces increased
access to Philippine air bases under the proposed
Temporary Access Agreement is unconstitutional and detrimental to the national interest. He also affirmed that Akbayan will participate in the global protest action against China scheduled the following day.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. CASTRO
Rep. Castro´s interpellation delved into Rep.
Bello´s (W.) proposed courses of action as far as the House is concerned in relation to the issue of the West Philippine Sea. He underscored that despite Rep. Bello´s statement on the necessity of a full congressional and executive support on the Philippine´s claim before an international tribunal, the resolution of the Philippine claim through compulsory arbitration before the United Nations is a tacit admission that the solution to such claim does not rest with the Philippine government; thus, any
declaration of congressional support will be a futile exercise. Reps. Castro and Bello further discussed the peaceful means that the country can do in promoting its national interest with regard to the conflict, with the latter stressing the lawmaking and oversight functions of Members of Congress in the formulation
and implementation of the country´s foreign policy as well as the political undertones of the legislative measures they pass in defense of the national interest.
(Source: HOUSE JOURNAL NO.2 pp. 69-70;73)

rows.author: H080;
rows.title_full: PLIGHT OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO WORKERS
rows.title_short: Failure Of The President To Mention Re: Ofws In His Sona
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. SEÑERES
In his speech, Rep. Señeres lamented that the
President´s SONA did not mention anything about
the plight of the overseas Filipino workers (OFW). He stressed that the Secretaries of Foreign Affairs and Labor and Employment were mandated by the Constitution and various laws to make the protection of OFWs their highest priority. He suggested that Congress summon them as well as the Vice President in his capacity as Presidential Adviser of OFWs, to explain why they had failed to advise the President of
the plight and problems of OFWs. He reminded the
Body that the increase in the gross domestic product and economic growth of the country was due to overseas Filipinos´ remittances.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. BICHARA
Reps. Bichara and Señeres, as former Philippine
Ambassadors to Lebanon and the United Arab
Emirates, respectively, agreed that 1) the DFA
Secretary should summon all ambassadors for a
command conference in order to remind them of their priorities; 2) ambassadors and labor attachÃ©s should coordinate more with each other; and 3) the Executive Department should increase the funds of the DFA which takes over from the DOLE as regards undocumented workers.
In addition, both Members concurred that the
Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA)
should look into the fact that some OFWs who
legally enter their host countries could lose their entitlement to OWWA funds once their contracts end. Lastly, they urged Congress to increase the budget allocation for OFW assistance.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. GARCIA (G.)
On motion of Rep. Banal, the Chair recognized
Rep. Gwendolyn F. Garcia who rued the fact that the SONA failed to cite the nation´s heroes who had been contributing billions of pesos to the economy. To her queries, Rep. Señeres opined that it was an honest inadvertence on the part of the President and claimed that the DFA and DOLE Secretaries and the Presidential Adviser on OFWs have probably been remiss in their job of advising the President on the plight of the OFWs. He and Rep. Garcia also agreed that Congress should summon the mentioned government officials as well as the other personalities who were involved in the writing of the President´s SONA to explain the matter.


INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
To the queries of Rep. Dela Cruz, Rep. Señeres
affirmed that the DFA and the DOLE are the two
main government agencies tasked to promote the
welfare of the OFWs and suggested the enactment of a law that would require ambassadors to play the role of surrogate parents to the OFWs within their area of jurisdiction. Rep. Dela Cruz pointed out however that the DFA and the DOLE should be blamed on the inadvertence of the President of not mentioning the contributions and the plight of the OFWs in his SONA. For his part, Rep. Señeres stated that he is not yet blaming the agencies mentioned but hoped that Congress would invite them to explain the matter.
(Source: HOUSE JOURNAL NO. 2, pp.74-75)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bichara, Garcia (G.) and dela Cruz. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules

rows.abstract:
Rep. Zamora discussed the collective views of
the Minority on the recent State of the Nation
Address (SONA) of President Benigno S. Aquino III, and focused his speech on the following: 1) the issue of corruption, particularly the Janet Lim Napoles PDAF scandal which the Minority intends to bring to the fore of a congressional inquiry; 2) the issue of poverty and how the country can achieve sustainable and inclusive economic growth by strengthening its
agricultural, industrial and financial sectors; and 3) the issue of Charter change which the Minority believes should give way to more pressing matters, like the peace talks, the country´s territorial dispute with China, the plight of Filipino workers here and abroad, and the need for universal health care and for
more accessible and equitable educational and
transport systems. To address the foregoing concerns, Rep. Zamora proposed, among others, several measures to prevent the illegal use of the PDAF and improve land reform in the country. He added that in the coming budget debates, the Minority will pose searching questions that confront the young and growing population, as
well as propose alternatives only for the record,
knowing that the Minority will never win in debates as well as in every voting. In ending, Rep. Zamora addressed the President personally by reminding him of the many things that still have to be accomplished in the remaining three
years of his term, such as curtailing poverty
especially in the provinces, developing the rising economy, and restoring peace in the streets. He said that the country does not only need a good President but a great President. INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Speaking in Filipino, Reps. Dela Cruz and
Zamora (R.) discussed the gaps that still have to be filled in the remaining three years of President Aquino´s term, most important of which are the structural reforms needed in the Philippine economy, politics and society. They agreed that the President was doing his best but could do more. They also opined that in the national budget deliberations, the legislature could implement line-item budgeting, scrap automatic and lump-sum appropriations, and
work for more resources for power and energy,
infrastructure, tourism, education, health and social services, and overseas Filipino workers.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
Rep. Rodriguez pointed out that the P-Noy
Administration had amply improved the country´s
credit rating and investment index. While Rep.
Zamora (R.) affirmed this, he said the President
should continue to strengthen his anti-corruption
campaign. Reps. Rodriguez and Zamora also discussed several concerns regarding agricultural development especially in terms of rice production, increased tourist arrivals, pork barrel scam, and Charter change. While Rep. Zamora stated that the Minority would file a House Resolution calling for an investigation into the pork barrel scam, he and Rep.
Rodriguez agreed that any proposed revision of the Constitution should include its economic and
political provisions. The latter even proposed a
constitutional shift to federalism so as to uplift the welfare of the people from Mindanao who are always at the bottom of human development index surveys in terms of life expectancy, education and income. Finally, the Members discussed the Bangsamoro framework agreement as well as the 2014 budgetary
share that is rightfully due to the Mindanao bloc, which the Minority Leader said he fully supports.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Roy V.
Señeres Sr. discussed with Rep. Zamora (R.) the
following concerns: 1) the proposal to criminalize labor contractualization; 2) the need for a policy or road map governing the eventual return to the country of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs); and 3) the huge amount of money borrowed from the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank to fund the government´s Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program.
(Source: HOUSE JOURNAL NO. 4, pp.78-79)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2013-07-29
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Dela Cruz Rodriguez(R.) and Seneres. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

Speaking in Filipino as well, Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. asked how successful the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) had been in addressing poverty. He urged his colleagues to take a serious look at the issue of pork barrel and to suspend the implementation of the PDAF until all the allegations related to the pork barrel scam shall have been addressed. OF REP. TEVES
Rep. Teves spoke about the conduct of the latest
mayoralty elections in Bayawan City where his party mate lost against a sole opponent. He explained that the voters got confused as to whether their candidate was listed as number one or number two in the ballot, and given the fact that 95% of his party members won, the complainants were willing to put under oath

rows.author: C072;
rows.title_full: MINDANAO PEACE PROCESS
rows.title_short: G R P - M N L F Peace Agreement
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. LOBREGAT
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Binay, Rep. Celso L. Lobregat from the First District of Zamboanga City talked about a recent incident involving Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF)leader Nur Misuari which disturbed the normalcy of Zamboanga City, when the MNLF patriarch threatened to declare Bangsamoro independence should the national government pursue the closure of the 1996 Government of the Republic of the Philippines (GRP)-MNLF Final Peace Accord. As he informed his colleagues that Zamboanga City voted twice for its exclusion from the Autonomous Region of Muslim Mindanao (ARMM), Rep. Lobregat requested the Office of the Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process (OPAPP) and the GRP negotiating panel to address the issues raised by Mr. Misuari about the tripartite review process and the Bangsamoro Framework Agreement, and reminded the Body, especially the incoming members of the
Special Committee on Peace, Reconciliation and
Unity, that the ARMM Organic Law already exists
and must be considered in drafting the Basic Law on the Bangsamoro. He concluded that a just and lasting peace in Mindanao can only be achieved if the government forges a peace agreement with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) in consultation with other stakeholders from Mindanao, like the MNLF.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BALINDONG
Reps. Balindong and Lobregat discussed the
latter´s position in favor of a meaningful and
strengthened Bangsamoro that will respect and not
include non-ARMM or non-Bangsamoro areas that
do not want to be part thereof, like Zamboanga City. Rep. Lobregat affirmed that he is against an independent Bangsamoro republic. They also tackled the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) on Ancestral Domain which the high court declared as unconstitutional, as well as the need to improve the ARMM Organic Act which, in
Rep. Lobregat´s view, was poorly implemented and
thus needed to be improved. Rep. Balindong however opined that the ARMM basic law was a failure because it did not address the root cause of the Mindanao conflict, which was an injustice to the Muslim Filipinos.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (R.)
Rep. Rodriguez discussed with and sought
clarifications from Rep. Lobregat on certain issues, including among others: the provisions of the 1996 GRP-MNLF Final Peace Accord which the
government had failed to meet, according to MNLF
Chairperson Misuari; and the forging of the proposed Bangsamoro Framework Agreement with the MILF within the context of the 1996 agreement with the MNLF, the 1976 Tripoli Agreement and the ARMM  Organic Act. Rep. Rodriguez then congratulated Rep. Lobregat and joined him in the referral of the latter´s speech to
the proper Committee.
* Amended as per Journal No. 6 of July 31, 2013
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOONG
Rep. Loong´s debate with Rep. Lobregat centered
on the latter´s reasons for opposing Mr. Misuari´s declaration of an independent Bangsamoro Republic, as well as on the proper procedure to be followed, including the laws and agreements to be duly considered, before the government tackles another peace agreement to address the Mindanao conflict.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 5, pp.21-22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Balindong, Rodriguez(R.) and Loong.  Referred to the Cttee. on Rules

rows.author: F012;
rows.title_short: Pork Barrel Scam / Call For An Investigation
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE OF REP. BARZAGA
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Elpidio F.
Barzaga Jr. referred to a news report published earlier in the day by the Philippine Star and Manila Bulletin stating that Rep. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz had furnished reporters with a portion of an alleged preliminary Commission on Audit (COA) report that was sent to him by a source, stating that the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) anomalies of more than P2 billion in pork barrel funds involved 28 Senators and 70 Representatives who are allies of the Aquino government. As he noted Rep. Dela Cruz´
presence in the Session Hall, he asked whether the latter really provided said information; was properly quoted by the newspapers; and had in his possession a copy of the preliminary COA report naming the 98 lawmakers. He stressed that the allegations would damage the reputation of the House because the information was given by a Member, and that it is Rep. Dela Cruz´ legal and moral obligation to stand up and be nterpellated on the floor.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. CASTRO
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Binay, Rep. Fredenil “Fred” H. Castro asked whether Rep. Barzaga was willing to file a resolution investigating the source of Rep. Dela Cruz´ information that was mentioned in his press release to finally determine whether the Members were involved in the pork barrel scam, as well as to protect their name and honor and that of the House as an institution. With Rep. Barzaga clarifying that to expedite proceedings, he would move for an investigation by the House into the accusations made by Rep. Dela Cruz, Rep. Castro said that he would join the motion
to clear the issue.
QUERY OF REP. GONZALES
Majority Leader Neptali M. Gonzales II inquired
whether Rep. Barzaga had already made a motion,
and to restate the same for the information of the Members.
MOTION OF REP. BARZAGA
Rep. Barzaga thereupon moved that the House
conduct an investigation to determine the truthfulness of the allegations made by Rep. Dela Cruz as published in the Philippine Star and Manila Bulletin....


REMARKS OF REP. GONZALES (N.)
Rep. Gonzales stated that Rep. Dela Cruz would
be given five minutes to explain his objection.
OBJECTION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
(Continuation)
Rep. Dela Cruz clarified that the reports that
were published the previous day and during the day were based on a partial COA report a copy of which was given to him by a source from the Commission itself. He mentioned what he had said during his press conference that he wanted to clear the name of the House from the many exposÃ©s being made by the Commission. He pointed out that the COA report did not mention particular names of legislators but merely stated that 244 projects were implemented
through the 15 NGOs participated in by 98
legislators; hence, he wanted COA to give all the
necessary information. He thereafter asked his
colleagues to join him in asking COA and the four
government agencies involved to bare all and not just certain names and pieces of information.
He also disclosed that he had already filed a
resolution calling for an inquiry into the use of the PDAF and other lump-sum funds under the national budget.
REP. BARZAGA´S POINT OF CLARIFICATION
Rep. Barzaga inquired whether Rep. Dela Cruz
was objecting to or joining his motion in order to ferret out the truth. Rep. Dela Cruz replied that he already filed a resolution on the matter even before Rep. Barzaga took the floor, which was the reason for his press conference. He then urged the Body to support his effort and clarified that he was not joining the motion
of Rep. Barzaga because he was the one who
initiated the information.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 6, p50-51)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2013-07-31
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Castro and Manifestation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F035;
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. GUNIGUNDO
In commemoration of the National Language
Month, Rep. Gunigundo, speaking in Filipino, dwelt on the status of the country´s national language and other Philippine languages and the government agency tasked to preserve and maintain the same. As he discussed the different native languages in the country and the recent pronouncement of the Komisyon ng Wikang Filipino (KWF) of changing the official name of the country from “Pilipinas” to “Filipinas” which is a clear violation of the Constitution
as only Congress is mandated to do so, he
stressed that it is about time to address the linguistic and cultural diversities and as such, the government should shift from a “one nation, one language” policy to one that recognizes the linguistic and cultural pluralism by establishing a Komisyon ng mga Wika sa
Pilipinas or Commission on Philippine Languages
and declaring “respect for all Philippine languages and cultures” as its guiding principle. Furthermore, he called on the Commission on Appointments to scrutinize the qualifications of the officials of the
Komisyon ng Wikang Filipino (KWF) on the spirit
and intent of Republic Act No. 7104 which created
said Commission.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PADILLA
To the concerns raised by Rep. Padilla, Rep.
Gunigundo stressed that Tagalog, Pilipino and Filipino are all mutually intelligible under one grammar. He pointed to the constitutional provision that the word “Filipino” is evolving and surmised that in time, as its vocabulary increases, it would no longer be in pure Tagalog because of the inclusion of other languages. He likewise noted that Filipino, as based in Tagalog and Pilipino, is now being widely used,
like in the delivery of the daily evening news as well as the President´s last State-of-the-Nation Address. For the record, he clarified that notwithstanding the provisions of Article XIV, second paragraph of Section 6, Filipino as the national language is now in place, and that the intent of Section 8 thereof, on the
promulgation of the 1987 Constitution in Filipino
and English, was duly complied with by its framers.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PADILLA
(Continuation)
As to Rep. Padilla´s suggestion to have a simultaneous translation of a regional language that would be used by a Member who would rise to speak on the floor, Rep. Gunigundo seconded the proposal adding that such service would make them express freely their thoughts and insights in their own native language. In closing, Rep. Padilla expressed his support to strengthen the Commission on Filipino Languages.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Rep. Atienza asked in Filipino whether the
Members could be united in his proposal to use the national language for the whole month of August in the plenary halls since it is stated in the Constitution and in the proclamation of the President. Rep. Gunigundo however invoked the freedom of speech whereby every Filipino may opt to speak also in English.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7, pp.13-14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2013-08-05
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Padilla and Atienza. Referred to the appropriate committee (per Journal) (Referred to the Cttee. on Basic Education per monitoring slip)

rows.author: H064;
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. ALEJANO
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Gary C. Alejano
from Party-List Magdalo recalled the Oakwood Mutiny which happened 10 years ago and which he surmised became an eye-opener to the public and a way for them to join and be victorious in the 2013 elections. He then thanked President Aquino for the amnesty he had granted to their group and also the Filipino people for trusting and believing in their cause and assured them of a continued honest and committed service. He expressed hope that there would be no need for another Oakwood incident because the Magdalo Party-List would be listening to soldiers´
grievances and would be part of the solution to the organization´s problems. In light of the perceived sources of distrust in the Legislature, he personally committed himself to defend the honor of the House by promoting public good and enhancing public trust.
In closing, he said that he is honored to be part of the House and that together with the seasoned and neophyte Members of the House, they can bring the country to greatness and march towards the “tuwid na daan.”
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 7, p.14)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2013-08-05
rows.remarks: Referred to Archives.

rows.author: H071;
rows.title_full: IMPLEMENTATION OF INTERIM MINDANAO ELECTRICITY MARKET
rows.title_short: Interim Mindanao Energy Market ( I M E M )
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. MASONGSONG
Rep. Masongsong discussed several issues regarding the continuing electricity power crisis in Mindanao and the impending implementation of the Interim Mindanao Electricity Market (IMEM). He said that to this day, Mindanao continues to experience rolling brownouts affecting both household and businesses but that several government initiatives have already been undertaken to mitigate and address the persisting power shortages such as the Mindanao Power Summit; and a Department Circular by the Department of Energy directing the Philippine Electricity Market Corporation (PEMC) to develop and implement an IMEM as a measure to immediately
address the power situation in Mindanao.
Rep. Masongsong stated that while he is in full
support of the government´s efforts to address the Mindanao power crisis, he had his reservations in the fast-track implementation of the IMEM. In ending, he reiterated the need to defer the implementation of the IMEM for further study and evaluation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Reps. Dela Cruz and Masongsong discussed the
requirements of Mindanao with regard to its power
generating capacity and whether there are particular sectors or individuals who are trying to rush the implementation of IMEM despite the particular power shortage in Mindanao.
Thereafter, on motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RODRIGUEZ (M.)
Reps. Rodriguez (M.) and Masongsong delved
on the power plants that are undergoing rehabilitation or repair and whether the IMEM is really the solution to the power crisis in Mindanao.They both agreed that the DOE should deploy the four remaining power barges to Mindanao instead of bidding them out, even as the latter qualified that repairs thereof should not be expensive. Stressing their concern for decreasing the cost of power, they also opined that renting or buying generator sets would mean big loans for electric cooperatives and
added cost to power rates. They then took note of the fact that the resolution of the problems faced by the power sector could easily be funded by the millions of Malampaya funds that had been transferred to the National Electrification Administration.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.7,pp.21-22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Dela Cruz and Rodriguez(M). Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H073;
rows.title_full: PLIGHT OF FILIPINO NURSES
rows.title_short: Health Care System And The Plight Of Filipino Nurses
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. PAQUIZ
Recognized by the Chair on a previous motion of
Rep. Gunigundo, Rep. Leah S. Paquiz of Ang Nars
Party-List spoke about the ills of the present health care system and the sad situation of nurses in the country. As she noted the neglect of health promotion and prevention of diseases, she also observed the exploitation of nurses in their desire to work. She underscored her Party-List´s vision of making the nursing sector an effective partner of the government in building a strong and healthy nation. She thereafter asked her colleagues to look into the present health care system and undertake policy and legal reforms to improve the same.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ILAGAN
Rep. Ilagan discussed with Rep. Paquiz several
issues affecting the country´s health care system in general and Filipino nurses in particular, including among others: 1) the practice of contract substitution victimizing health workers who go abroad, and the
steps being done to address the problem; 2) the
discrimination that Filipino nurses have to endure when working abroad; 3) the proliferation of nursing schools in the country and the quality of graduates they produce; 4) the effect of health care privatization to poor and middle class families; and 5) the implementation of the “no home birthing” policy.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ZAMORA (R.)
Recognized by the Chair, Minority Leader
Ronaldo B. Zamora advised Rep. Paquiz to inquire
into the allocation under the 2014 proposed national budget for preventive and curative health care programs. They also discussed the problem of labor contractualization in the nursing profession and the stand of Rep. Paquiz against the privatization of hospitals in the country. Rep. Zamora pointed out that at the appropriate time, the Members would have an intensive discussion with the representatives from the Department of Health (DOH) regarding preventive and curative health care.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. KHO
On motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the Chair next
recognized Rep. Elisa “Olga” T. Kho who first
commended Rep. Paquiz for articulating the sad
plight of Filipino nurses. As a former provincial
health officer of Masbate Provincial Health Office, she aired her concerns on the dismal salaries of health workers and the lack of full implementation of the Magna Carta for Health Workers. She pointed out that it is high time that salaries of public doctors and nurses should be evaluated and for Congress to revisit the Salary Standardization Law for health
workers to prevent brain drain in the country´s health sector. She also disagreed with the contention of Rep. Ilagan in support of “no home birthing” policy because she believes that there is no substitute for experienced traditional hilot but proposed further education and obstetric trainings to improve their craft. With regard to the proposed building of more hospitals, she opined that the focus should be on
primary health care prevention to lessen problems on hospital maintenance and manpower.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. GUNIGUNDO
Reps. Gunigundo and Paquiz discussed the reason the DOH is proposing the privatization of
government hospitals in the country and the latter´s contrary opinion on the proposal of DOH Secretary Ona that privatization of the Philippine Orthopedic Hospital in Quezon City would improve its services and facilities and help many poor patients.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 8,pp.19 & 29)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps.Ilagan, Zamora(R), Kho and Gunigundo. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_short: Transparency And Reforms On Budgetary Allocations
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz focused on the country´s
budgetary process involving the funding and
implementation of projects financed by the
lawmakers´ Priority Development Assistance Fund
(PDAF) or the so-called equalization fund that
constitutes a measly one percent of the total national budget for 2013. He stressed the need for the public to be properly informed of the beneficial uses of the said fund but more importantly, of the purposes of specific lump sum and automatic expenditure items
in the general appropriations act which form almost 60% of the national budget, which include the items on debt servicing, pension and gratuity fund, and unprogrammed fund. After explaining on how Congress has allegedly
become a convenient scapegoat of Executive
agencies and project auditors for their poor
implementation and monitoring of PDAF-financed
projects, Rep. Dela Cruz also elaborated on how the Commission on Audit (COA) has made biased and
inaccurate pronouncements on corruption in
Congress. He thereafter asked for a speedy and just inquiry on the “pork barrel” issue and a submission of complete agency reports on suspected anomalous projects and transactions. He also asked for reformsin the congressional allocation system through the adoption of line-item budgeting method, coursing of
funds through accountable officers and offices
instead of through foundations and nongovernment
organizations (NGOs), and the removal of automatic and lump sum appropriations in the national budget. He proposed to review the COA Law to guard against partisan politics and ensure accountability and stressed that Congress can retain its footing only through self-cleansing and reform.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BARZAGA
To the clarificatory questions of Rep. Elpidio F.
Barzaga Jr. whom the Chair recognized, Rep. Dela
Cruz emphasized that he did not want to remove the “pork barrel” system but to reform it through such means as he had enumerated in his speech. He said that during his one-and-a-half term in the 14th Congress, he placed his PDAF in government hospitals, schoolbuildings, and educational funds of local government units and not in foundations or NGOs.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.8 p.24)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-08-06)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Barzaga. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: H068;
rows.title_full: RESETTLEMENT PROGRAM FOR INFORMAL SETTLER - FAMILIES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gutierrez talked about the issue of informal
settlers and their human rights by underscoring the State´s constitutional and legal mandate to provide for a continuing urban land reform and housing program as well as to respect and protect the right of the poor against forcible eviction, which were given teeth with the passage of the Urban Development and Housing Act of 1992. He thereafter focused on the
government´s “on-site, in-city relocation” policy
governing resettlement and the primary role given to the “people´s plan” as proposed by the relocatees themselves with the assistance of government agencies concerned in the implementation thereof. He opined that these principles are crucial in ensuring the sustainability and viability of future
resettlement projects, and stressed the need for the continuous monitoring of the implementation of the government´s relocation program and for the integration of said principles into the framework for socialized housing program.

(SOURCE: House Journal No. 9, p.22)
rows.status: Committee Report filed on 2014-10-27
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: H025;
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the Chair
recognized Rep. Edgar R. Erice from the Second
District of Caloocan City who spoke about the
urgency of suspending the conduct of the
Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) elections scheduled in
October until the government shall have decided
whether to totally abolish the current SK system or to merely reform it. He mentioned several concerns, including among others: 1) his bill seeking the abolition of SK; 2) how the present SK system has introduced to the youth and inculcated in them a culture of corruption and a distorted perspective of public service and governance; 3) the positive contributions to the youth´s political development of the defunct Kabataang Barangay (KB) system which he became part of during his youth; and 4) the reported stance of the Commission on Elections chairperson himself convincing the President to
certify as urgent the pending bills seeking to
postpone the SK election.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. FARIÑAS
Rep. Fariñas debated with Rep. Erice on how
best to address the problems besetting the present SK system, suggesting in particular the importance for older politicians and government officials to set better examples in governance and public service for the youth to emulate as well as to educate the people in electing better government officials. He said that the SK system should not be blamed for producing corrupt SK officials in Caloocan City because the same cannot be said of the SK officials throughout
the country. He also mentioned that his son is the SK Federation President in Ilocos Norte but has never benefited from his salary as he uses the same to fund his SK projects. In reply to the issues raised, Rep. Erice argued against the participation of very young Filipinos in local politics, citing the adverse exposure of the
youth to a political system that is dictated by
traditional politicians and a political exercise that has degenerated into the use of public funds for personal political purposes. He reiterated his proposal for a deferment of the SK poll scheduled in October until such time that Congress has come up with a better
alternative to the SK as a venue for the youth´s
political participation. Nonetheless, he acknowledged the contention of Rep. Fariñas that in molding young politicians, the country´s older and more politically experienced leaders should set better examples worthy of emulation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RIDON
Rep. Ridon inquired on Rep. Erice´s proposal to
defer the SK election and the issue of abolishing the SK on the basis that the SK has become a breeding ground for future corrupt leaders. He claimed that instead of deferring the SK election and castigating the corrupt practices of young political leaders, the
proposal should instead focus on an enabling law
implementing the constitutional provision against
political dynasty whose premise has even predated
the SK on the issues of political cronyism and
corruption. Rep. Erice clarified that the absence of an antipolitical dynasty law could be a contributory factor to the issue of prevalent traditional politics and corruption in the SK and reiterated his stand against allowing the youth, aged 15 to 17, to participate in
politics that involves the disposal of huge public funds and the waste of billions of pesos allocated for annual SK projects. He affirmed that while the call for SK abolition is also tantamount to the removal of youth representation and participation in public
office, there is a need to create a new and alternative political venue for youth participation that would free young politicians from the dictates and influence of traditional politicians.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 9, pp.22-23)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2013-08-07
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Farinas and Ridon. Referred to the Committee on Local Government.

rows.author: F103;
rows.title_short: 7.5% Economic Growth And The Filipino Farmer
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Guanlao spoke about the millions of small
farmers in the Philippines. Despite feeding the
nation, he stated that they continue to suffer from high rice production costs, low palay farm-gate prices, harvest-destroying calamities, net incomes way below the poverty threshold, cheaper
imported/smuggled rice, and insufficient support
services. To address their deep and unchanging
poverty, he asked the government to keep agricultural production costs low, institutionalize rural credit assistance, redirect funds such as those of the
Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program to rice
productivity programs, and pass laws on good
governance and sound fiscal management. He
pointed out that formulating and implementing rural development policies was crucial to national growth. He urged the Body to keep the farmers´ plight in mind during the budget deliberations.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAEZ
Rep. Guanlao initially clarified to Rep. Cresente
C. Paez, whom the Chair next recognized, that he
worked in a rural bank but his father was a farmer and his family worked in the farm. They then discussed the budget allocation for the agricultural sector under the 2014 proposed national budget. Given that the agricultural sector badly needs government support, Rep. Guanlao proposed that part of the budget allocation for the CCT program should
be subsidized to the peasant sector in order to sustain its growth and development. He also urged his colleagues to look into programs and projects that will truly develop the agricultural sector.
Continuing with his interpellation, Rep. Paez
suggested that instead of a single-digit interest rate on credit loans, the government should expand the access of small farmers to agricultural credit and simplify the loan documentary requirements and procedures. For his part, Rep. Guanlao reiterated his proposal that part of the CCT allocation should be subsidized to the agricultural sector considering that
the subsidies for post-harvest facilities under the 2014 budget have decreased. Finally, both Members discussed the issues of adulteration of fertilizer bags and rice smuggling in the Bureau of Customs (BOC), with Rep. Guanlao urging Congress to inquire into the matter. He also
suggested that instead of bidding out the smuggled rice, it should be given to the National Food Authority (NFA) or the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) for distribution to proper beneficiaries.
EXTENSION OF THE PRIVILEGE HOUR
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BONDOC
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Gunigundo, Rep. Guanlao agreed with the concerns
raised by Rep. Juan Pablo “Rimpy” P. Bondoc that
allocating a portion of the CCT Program to smallscale farmers might result in expanded money supply which, without the corresponding increase in production of goods, could possibly result in higher prices of commodities. They also agreed that instead, the Departments of Agriculture, and Budget and Management should reallocate subsidies for postharvest
facilities to lower the production risks of
farmers and in support of the agriculture industry. Thereafter, Rep. Gunigundo moved for the recognition of Rep. Walden F. Bello for his
interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BELLO (W.)
Rep. Bello raised concern on the ill effects of
trade liberalization to the agriculture industry, and the need for Congress to initiate a review of the country´s commitments under the World Trade Organization and other agreements that affect Philippine agriculture. He also discussed with Rep. Guanlao the country´s inclusion in the proposed Southeast Asian nations´ “one integrated market” when it is not yet prepared to become a member thereof.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.9, pp.29-30)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-08-07)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Paez, Bondoc and Bello(W). Referred to the Committee on Agriculture.

rows.author: G034;
rows.title_full: UNMASKING THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE ARREST OF REP. DIMAPORO A.
rows.title_short: Demolition Job Against Rep. Abdullah Dimaporo
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized
Rep. Imelda Quibranza Dimaporo from the First District of Lanao del Norte who denounced the
black propaganda being hurled against her husband
Rep. Abdullah D. Dimaporo by their political opponents in connection with his alleged involvement in the infamous fertilizer scam. She enumerated the names of the persons allegedly responsible behind the demolition job against her husband, led by Immigration Associate Commissioner Abdullah “Dabs” Mangotara, and explained that her purpose for doing so is for the concerned government agencies to act on
their alleged participation in criminal and nefarious activities and to unmask what she claimed as “wolves” in the Administration´s political party. She emphasized that in providing information to the public, she is not asking for any special treatment in the case of Rep. Dimaporo (A.) but is only seeking fairness, justice and equity considering that his case
does not concern a legal issue but is political in nature. She stated that she and her family will stand up to protect the will and mandate of the people of Lanao del Norte and prevent Associate Commissioner Mangotara and his cohorts from usurping the political office of the Second District of Lanao del Norte through criminal and undemocratic means.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. ROMUALDEZ
Informed by the Chair that Rep. Dimaporo (I.) had already taken her seat ad being cognizant of Rep. Dimaporo's (A.) situation, Rep. Romualdez manifested his request for the House leadership to reconsider its pronounced hands-off policy in the case of Rep. Dimaporo (A.). He contended that the crime to be charged should be malversation of public funds which is bailable, and not the complex crime of malversation through falsification of public documents.
The Chair noted the manifestation.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 10, pp. 20-21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Romualdez. Referred to the Cttee. on Rules.

rows.author: F054;
rows.title_full: COMMENDED THE FIBA GILAS PILIPINAS BASKETBALL TEAM
rows.title_short: Recognition Of Gilas Pilipinas' Victory In The 27th F I B A - Asia Championship
rows.abstract:
Rep. Puno lauded the Gilas Pilipinas National
Basketball Team for winning the silver medal in the 27th FIBA Asia Championship Games thus enabling them to play in the 17th FIBA World Cup in Spain the following year. He took note of their teamwork, strong determination, unwavering commitment and hard training as he enumerated their names; and stressed that their victory was the strongest finish of a Filipino basketball team since 1985. He acknowledged the efforts of their coaches and financial sponsors; the support and encouragement of the Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas (SBP) and the
Philippine Basketball Association (PBA); the
House´s approval of his bill granting Filipino
citizenship to Gilas player Marcus Douthit and the Senate´s filing of a counterpart measure; and the support of the fans and the entire nation. Thereafter, Rep. Puno showed a video
presentation about the team.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Subsequently, the Chair recognized Rep.
Jonathan A. Dela Cruz who urged Congress to
naturalize at least two more players identified by the SBP for the national team to serve as back-up players, as he recalled that Marcus Douthit was injured in the Philippines-Korea game in the recent FIBA Asia Championship. This, he explained, will help sustain the country´s world-class performance in the global basketball arena and realize its collective dream of an Asian and even world championship. Rep. Puno expressed support for the naturalization of athletes especially those with exceptional merit and ability.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 10, pp.29-30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_full: COMFORT WOMEN
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair next
recognized Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan of Gabriela
Party-List who reminded the Body of the struggle of so-called Filipina comfort women. She pointed out that it was 20 years ago that the first of the so-called Filipina comfort women surfaced and testified on their systematic sexual slavery at the hands of Japanese soldiers during World War II and called on the Japanese government to formally acknowledge and accept responsibility, apologize, and give them compensation. She rued the fact that these victims -- most of whom are weak and sickly and some of whom have already died -- still had to receive justice despite legislative measures filed, mass actions held,
and coordination and liaison work done by the
Gabriela Women´s Party. She stressed that the Philippine government and the House of Representatives are culprits to the slow
justice that these grandmothers are suffering from because of their failure to issue even a statement of condemnation for the insults hurled against comfort women by the mayor of Osaka City. She then asked her colleagues to right a wrong that was committed many years ago.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10, p.30)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G118;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Garin cited a recent Supreme Court
decision declaring the coconut levy fund as public money and therefore public property which Congress has to protect with utmost vigilance to ensure that it only benefits the coconut farmers and the coconut industry. She discussed the possible ways of channeling the fund back to the coconut farmers, including among others 1) paying back the farmers; 2) allowing the national government to pour in money and restructure the Philippine Coconut
Authority; 3) using the funds to stabilize the price of copra; 4) creating local coconut councils in every local government unit; and 5) creating farmercentered processing zones. She reminded the Body that the fund belongs to the coconut farmers and is neither a gift, a product of luck nor a free ticket for public spending, and that both Congress and Malacañang should use the money to improve the lives only of these people and no one else.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOONG
Recognized by the Char, Rep. Tupay T. Loong
discussed with Rep. Garin (S.) certain issues
regarding the administration of the coconut levy
fund, with the former lamenting the fact that the
coconut farmers in most Muslim communities in the
Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao have not
benefited from it. He also joined the call of Rep. Garin for Congress and the concerned agencies from the Executive branch to look into ways that would guarantee that the fund will solely benefit its intended beneficiaries.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BONDOC
Rep. Bondoc´s interpellation of Rep. Garin (S.)
focused on his agreement with the latter´s advocacy that the coconut levy fund should fully benefit the coconut industry. This, as he cited the conclusion of an American economist from his study of African agricultural economies that the government usually redirects the financial and economic surpluses produced by a certain agricultural sector to other purposes thus depriving the actual sector that produced the surpluses of the support it needs to become globally competitive.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. KHO
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Elisa
“Olga” T. Kho inquired if there is a complete list of original coconut farmers who have contributed to the coconut levy fund so they could be consulted as to how they want to use their monies. Rep. Garin (S.) described the problem of identifying the original fund contributors but mentioned that there are a few
existing registered coconut farmers´organizations
which are regularly consulting with the
Department of Agricuture, the Philippine Coconut Authority and other related agencies about the matter.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAEZ
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Cresente C. Paez
inquired on the best way to manage the coconut levy fund and challenged Rep. Garin (S.) to file a bill setting the parameters that would guide the management and disbursement of the fund so as to ensure that it will truly benefit the coconut farmers and avoid the danger of its utilization turning out into another scam.
Rep. Garin stated that while the fund is presently under the control of the Presidential Commission on Good Government, the Administration will need experts from the fields of investments and agriculture as well as members from different government sectors to ensure the proper management and allocation of the fund.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10, pp.30-31)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2013-08-12
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Loong, Bondoc, Kho and Paez. Referred to the Committee on Agriculture and Food.

rows.author: G012;
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. BATAOIL
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair
recognized Rep. Bataoil from the Second District of Pangasinan who, speaking in Filipino, initially congratulated the Gilas Pilipinas Basketball Team for winning the silver medal in the recent FIBA Asia Championship Games and once again putting the country in the map of world sports. In celebration of the National Language Month, Rep. Bataoil talked about the subject of baybayin and its essence as the written language to be used in treading the straight path. He expressed belief that the country´s national language which includes both spoken or auditory and written or visual, need to flourish before the people could walk through the straight path of success. As he underscored the importance of Filipino written language, he asked whether the people will allow the written language to be included in the list of endangered alphabets and become totally extinct, or to be propagated and taught as their legacy to the next generation of Filipinos.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.10, p.31)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2013-08-12
rows.remarks: Referred to the Cttee. on Basic Education

rows.author: H088;
rows.title_full: BOMBING INCIDENTS IN THE CITIES OF CAGAYAN DE ORO AND COTABATO
rows.abstract:
In his maiden speech in Congress which he dedicated in memory of the victims of the latest bombing incidents in Mindanao, Rep. Pagdilao called on the government and the people to unite in the fight against crime and terrorism as he underscored several pertinent issues describing the current state of the government´s efforts against terrorism. He cited in particular the bombing incidents that happened in Mindanao within a span of three weeks, causing a number of fatalities and injured; the government´s
disregard of the adverse effect of the travel advisories issued by foreign embassies against traveling to Mindanao; and the failure of law enforcers to identify and apprehend the perpetrators responsible for the said incidents.
Rep. Pagdilao underscored the reactive stance
and lack of coordination among government agencies in addressing the spate of bombings in the country as a vicious cycle that needs to be overturned with the creation of a single agency of government to address the issue of terrorism. As he stated that it is about time to take a proactive approach in addressing terrorism
and crimes, Rep. Pagdilao suggested, among
others, that Congress should review the implementation of the Human Security Act of 2007 and that people should be motivated to supply evidence to authorities.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BATAOIL
Reps. Pagdilao and Bataoil discussed the implementation of the Human Security Act since its enactment in 2007, with the former urging Congress to perform its oversight function over Executive agencies, and the latter suggesting a wholistic approach in solving the country´s terrorism problem. They also tackled the police operational procedures on preserving crime evidence, as exemplified in the case of the
Cagayan de Oro bombing incident. They agreed that
holding and release procedures should be improved, and that a resolution in aid of legislation should be filed to inquire into the enforcement of the Human Security Act.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11, pp.11 & 12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bataoil. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H065;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza said that he filed a resolution on the pork barrel funds because Congress should be sensitive to the public clamor for its suspension. He recalled that Majority Leader Neptali M. Gonzales II had commented that the same was not in order and Rep. Atienza should not get his allocations if he did not want it. He however stressed in Filipino that what
he did was the most relevant way to clean the name of the House; the issue involved not private but public funds; and the Members should treasure the democratic way and respect each one´s right to take and defend a position. He pointed out that the Liberal Party, of which he used to be a member, fell apart because of the ignorance and arrogance of its leaders.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DEL MAR
Rep. Del Mar expressed support for the sentiments
of his colleague and said that the filing of said
resolution was in order. Nevertheless, he opined that Rep. Gonzales is not one to prevent anyone from speaking his mind and the problem between the two Members could be miscommunication. For his part, Rep. Atienza stressed that the Majority Leader should not have made the aforecited statements in public. As he stressed his desire for Reps. Gonzales and Atienza to get together as what they had was just a clear case of misunderstanding, Rep. Del Mar said that the Members should respect each other and come up with a decision of whether to implement, suspend
or abolish the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF). He condemned the alleged misuse of the pork barrel by certain Members as against those who used the fund to help their constituents, especially the needy.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 11, pp.12-13)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-08-13)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Del Mar. Point of Order by Reps. Barzaga and Remarks by Rep. Gonzales.

rows.author: B015;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gonzales clarified that he never said that
Rep. Atienza´s resolution was out of order because any Member is entitled to file one, and that he never bullied a colleague as he was always in the front line when it comes to defending the integrity of the House. He said that he merely responded to the queries
raised by the media on his reaction to the resolution as well as to the suggestion of certain quarters to suspend the release of PDAF funds. He added that he also merely explained that the resolution would be referred to the appropriate Committee for proper action
and recalled having expressed hope that the resolution would be voted upon favorably, otherwise, it would not be deliberated in plenary. He thereafter clarified that he also suggested that since the House has already started the 2014 national budget deliberations,
then concerns about the release of the second
half of the 2013 and the 2014 PDAFs could be raised therein. Subsequently, Rep. Gonzales stressed that his statement “kung ayaw mo, huwag mo” was not personally directed to Rep. Atienza but was a general comment to all those who wish to suspend the release of PDAF. He admitted to having even suggested that there is no need to wait for Congress to approve a resolution suspending the release of PDAF as those
who do not wish to avail of the fund allocation could just simply not submit a list of identified projects. He added that they could not tell their constituents that just because their PDAF is suspended, and so is their assistance.
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE
OF REP. GONZALES
(Continuation)
Rep. Gonzales thereafter asked whether he was
not entitled to defend his honor, and pointed anew to his constituents who seek assistance for basic needs like hospitalization At this point, the Chair reminded Rep. Gonzales that he still had two minutes of his time. Finally, Rep. Gonzales restated that he never said that Rep. Atienza or his resolution was out of order
and stressed that in all his years as a Member of
Congress, he was always the first to defend the integrity of the House.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.11, pp.13-14)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-08-13)

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: INTERNATIONAL YOUTH DAY
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Durano, the Chair recognized
Rep. Terry L. Ridon from Party-List Kabataan who
spoke about the plight of the youth in connection
with the celebration of the International Youth Day the previous day. He thereafter cited the problems  besetting education in the country, which include the deregulated tuition and other fees, dwindling state funding to public education, and antistudent policies
such as the “no late payment and no permit, no
exam” policy. He noted that the government´s proposed solution was to add two years of basic education or the K to 12 Program and the so-called rationalization of funding for public higher education. He then challenged the youth and student leaders to reinvigorate the youth movement in order to uphold and defend their rights, welfare and interests and the other sectors of the nation. In support thereof, he asked the Members to pass prostudent laws, such as the Student´s Rights and Welfare Law;
fight corruption; rescind apathy; and rekindle the youthful idealism that made them leaders that they are today.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 11, p. 21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F071;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Teves spoke about the proper use of
calamity funds and thereafter adverted to a local
newspaper article published in his province which
reported about the alleged P1 billion-anomaly in
Negros Oriental when calamity funds were released
during the time that typhoon Sendong and an
earthquake struck his province in December 2011
and February 2012, respectively. He thereafter asked his colleagues to review how calamity funds are to be released, used, monitored and safeguarded for the best interest of the Filipino people.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SALIMBANGON
Rep. Salimbangon asked clarificatory questions
on the veracity of the data published in the local newspaper. After affirming the details of the contract, Rep. Teves stressed that 1) projects involving P50 million or more should first pass the Department of Public
Works and Highways (DPWH); 2) some of his
constituents had already filed pertinent complaints in the Office of the Ombudsman in view of the aforecited disallowance; and 3) the President did not approve of the project that he ordered the release of a negative Special Allotment Release Order (SARO). Reps. Teves and Salimbangon then agreed that guidelines should be set on the use of calamity funds from the Office of the President, and that Congress
should investigate the matter.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 12, p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Salimbangon. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.title_full: MILITARIZATION OF MINING ACTIVITIES IN NUEVA VIZCAYA
rows.title_short: Escalating Military Operations In Nueva Vizcaya
rows.abstract:
Rep. Padilla called attention to the escalation of military operations in the municipality of Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya because of the strong resistance to the mining operations of Royalco Resources Ltd (Royalco) therein. He disclosed that soldiers from the 86th Infantry Battalion dismantled the barricades put up by residents, most of whom belong to migrant tribes, to prevent the entry of mining equipment and
personnel. Describing how the residents were
terrorized, he asked whether the soldiers acted within the bounds of their mandated functions. In
conclusion, he stressed that the cultural communities simply wanted to harness, save, and protect their ancestral domain.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Gunigundo, Rep. Roy V. Señeres Sr. and his
colleague discussed on removing the military and
mining operations in the area, invoking existing laws to justify the same; the following up of 
the Secretary of the National Defense´s action on the matter; and conducting a congressional inquiry on the reasons behind the aforecited military action.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.13, p.18)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Seneres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H084;
rows.title_short: In Defense Of Former Cong. Way Kurat
rows.abstract:
Rep. Zamora (M.) rose to defend her father,
former Congressman and now Compostela Valley
Vice Governor Manuel “Way Kurat” Zamora, who
had been reported by the Commission on Audit
(COA) as having received more than P3 billion in
Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF)
allocations in 2007. She cited pronouncements of the former and incumbent Secretaries of the Department of Budget and Management that her father was a victim of clerical error and/or misappreciation of documents. She clarified that the amount went to the maintenance of national roads through the Department of Public Works and not to her father´s office, their district, or their pockets. Subsequently, Rep. Zamora (M.) decried the irresponsibility, unfairness, and inaccuracy not only of the COA but also of mass media and the social network. She said she was waiting for the COA´s recognition and admission of its mistake.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. BELLO (S.)
Clarifying that he would just make a manifestation, Rep. Bello vouched for the integrity of his former colleague representing Compostela Valley and said he was a man of honor and simple taste. He then sought a public apology from the COA.
The Chair took note of the same.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
On motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the Chair
recognized Rep. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz who agreed
that the COA acted irresponsibly and its Chairperson should publicly apologize for tarnishing the honor and integrity of the former Congressman. He urged the Members to ask COA Chairperson Grace Pulido-Tan to exit from her position or be impeached.
The Chair took note of the same.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. CORTUNA
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Juliet R. Cortuna
inquired on the House leadership´s position on the matter as she stressed that it was not just one Member but the entire legislature that was being attacked. She called upon the Majority as well as the Minority to file a resolution in defense of the institution.
The Chair took note of the same.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 13, pp.18-19)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-08-27)
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Reps. Bello(S), Dela Cruz and Cortuna . Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.title_full: MV ST. THOMAS AQUINAS MISHAP IN CEBU
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the Chair
subsequently recognized Rep. Raul V. Del Mar from
the First District of Cebu City who sought
government action on the recent collision of MV St. Thomas Aquinas and MV Sulpicio Express Siete in Talisay City on August 16, 2013. He read into the records various reports detailing trauma, injury, and death among the victims of the tragedy. He asked the Department of Transportation and Communications and Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) to expedite its investigation and submit the results thereof; and the
House to relay its support and sympathy for the
victims´ families as well as seek assistance for them from the national and local agencies concerned. After lauding the voluntary and rescue work of private and public individuals and agencies, he stressed that the
PCG must prosecute those responsible for the
incident and enforce stricter rules on public safety especially in accident-prone areas.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.13, p.19)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F122;
rows.title_short: Safeguard In The Use Of P D A F
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz said that after the rally held in
Luneta on August 26, 2013 to denounce the so-called “pork system,” Congress should now listen to the people´s wish for the abolition of the PDAF and all other forms of “pork,” including that of the President´s, and pinpoint who are responsible and accountable to the public´s money. He opined that the Legislature should adopt the line-item budgeting and scrutinize the special provisions in the national budget. He thereafter referred to the speech delivered
by Rep. Maria Carmen S. Zamora in the previous
day´s session on the irresponsible and unfair
assertions of Commission on Audit Chairperson
Grace Pulido-Tan against her father, former
Representative and now Vice-Governor Manuel
“Way Kurat” Zamora. He said that Chairperson
Pulido-Tan committed a graver crime when she
accepted raw and unvalidated data that tainted the integrity of certain people and institutions like Congress. He added that COA should have identified and held accountable the Department of Budget and Management´s officials for the excessive release of funds. In closing, he asked Chairperson Grace Pulido-Tan and her acolyte Commissioner Heidi Mendoza to apologize for coming out with that kind of audit report or just resign if they would not do so.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 14, p.13)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-08-28)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: MILLION PEOPLE MARCH
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon explained that his speech intends to
underscore the challenges the Filipino people is faced with after the “Million People March” at the Luneta last August 26, 2013 where the people had displayed show of force and strong objection against the pork barrel system and the sytematic wastage of public funds. He adverted to President Aquino´s pronouncement on the issue of abolishing the pork barrel system as merely a political ploy to undermine and put cosmetic changes to the efforts of the people for genuine social change, good governance, and an
end to congressional impasse on the PDAF
investigations. He thereafter called on the Members of the 16th Congress to take heed of what the Filipino people had started at the “Million People March,” by similarly taking action on the challenges of systemic corruption of public funds that could have improved
the welfare of the people with better services for public health and education. He stated that the Members can start taking action specifically on the impending budgetary cuts on about 79 out of 110 State Colleges and Universities in the proposed 2014 National Budget. Rep. Ridon then enjoined the Members to be steadfast in their belief in the power of the people.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.14, p.16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F100;
rows.title_full: ABOLITION OF LUMP SUM APPROPRIATIONS
rows.title_short: Power Of The Purse Of Congress
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized
Rep. Neri J. Colmenares from Party-List Bayan
Muna who sought the abolition of the lump-sum
amounts in the budget and the need for Congress to take back its constitutional power over the purse. Rep. Colmenares further argued on several issues affecting the exercise of congressional power to appropriate, particularly in the use of: 1) Lump-Sum Amount appropriations;          2) Unprogrammed Funds; 3) Special Purpose Funds; 4) Overall Savings (Fund) of Departments and Agencies; and 5) Re-enacted Budget. He maintained that the circumvention and misuse of these “budgeting mechanisms” have led to
continuing instances of graft and corruption, the
presidential abuse of the powers of Congress over the purse, and the contravention of the decision by Congress in the realignment of budgetary appropriations approved in the plenary.
Rep. Colmenares thereafter underscored and
enumerated his main contentions against the Lump
Sum Amount appropriations. He adverted in particular to the substantial total amount of Lump Sum Amount appropriations in the National Budget for “Presidential Pork”; the Priority Development Assistance Fund as appropriated in the National Budget being “dwarfed” by the amount of the President´s “pork”; the President being empowered by a special provision in the regular budgets of departments and agencies allowing him to realign budgetary funds and
without the need for any congressional approval; and that Congress being relegated only to the plenary deliberations of the National Budget. He also maintained that the PDAF is a form of “presidential pork.” To further emphasize his arguments, Rep. Colmenares pointed out that for every lump-sum appropriations approved by Congress, the same constitutes a diminution of its power over the purse and its power to appropriate; however, for every itemization
of the lump-sum amounts, he explained that Congress is regaining the “lump sum allocations” used for presidential pork. He thereafter proposed for the abolition of the Lump Sum Amount appropriations in order that Congress, specifically the House of Representatives,
can regain its power over the purse.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BARZAGA
On Rep. Barzaga´s query regarding the definition
of “pork barrel.” Rep. Colmenares replied that an
academic definition of “pork barrel” is that it is a “congressional insertion” to refer the use of lump sum amount of appropriations in the National Budget and/or the authority to identify and determine development projects, the amount, and beneficiaries; also includes the use of public funds for the purpose of patronage politics; and opined that “pork barrel” constitutes also the “presidential power and prerogative” of the President to decide, approve or disapprove the allocation of funds to the contravention of the power of Congress over the purse. Rep. Colmenares then answered Rep. Barzaga´s questions on other issues, including the popular definition of the term pork barrel; why lump-sum appropriations controlled by governors and mayors should be considered as another form of pork barrel; how lump sum funds undermine the Legislature´s constitutional
power of the purse; why parliamentary tradition
should not be used as an excuse to continue the
pork barrel system; and the absence of Supreme
Court ruling on the constitutionality of lump sum
funds. Rep. Colmenares also reaffirmed the position of Party-List Bayan Muna favoring the abolition of the pork barrel of both Congress and the President even as some of its Representatives received PDAF allocations
in the 15th Congress. He stressed that the discretion to spend public funds should not be solely given to one person. The interpellation further focused on how the use of PDAF has been abused, and how Bayan Muna properly disposed of its fund during the 15th Congress, particularly for education and health services without using NGOs nor LGUs, and how similarly, the pork barrel can be availed of in the 16th Congress
without graft, corruption or abuse. They also discussed political patronage insofar as the lump-sum appropriations are concerned, and the need to specify certain items contained therein because of the huge amount of money involved and which cannot be the subject matter of a congressional inquiry.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. CASTRO
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Alvarez
(F.), Rep. Fredenil “Fred” H. Castro´s interpellation centered on the President´s mandated authority over the Lump-Sum appropriations, and which he pointed out is provided by the law that Congress itself
approved. Rep. Castro pointed out that it is the duty and responsibility of the Members of the House to demand itemized budget or to scrutinize lump sum budget from the Executive Department. Otherwise, he said that they would be the ones who would be remiss in performing their obligations.
(SOURCE: House Journal No. 15, pp.18,19 & 22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Barzaga and Castro. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: US PLANNED ATTACK AGAINST SYRIA
rows.title_short: Planned U S Attack On Syria
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bello underscored the national interest of
the Philippines in the light of United States President Barack Obama´s request for congressional approval to undertake punitive actions against the Syrian government for the alleged use of chemical weapons resulting to the deaths of hundreds of its citizens. He argued that the reprehensible deed, whether committed by the Assad regime or by the Syrian Opposition, does not merit any unilateral aggression from the United States in the absence of a clear legal
justification against a sovereign country; and more so, the United States does not have the approval of the United Nations Security Council. He stated that the planned unilateral action of the United States government would further compound the sufferings of the Syrian population where the ongoing civil war had already resulted to more than hundred thousands killed and numerous Syrians fleeing their country.
(In view of preserving the country´s national interest with the presence of thousands of Filipinos in Syria and millions of OFWs in the Middle East, Rep. Bello made the following proposals: 1) for President Benigno S. Aquino III to signify and assert the strong opposition of the country to President Obama´s planned military strike against Syria; 2) for the Philippine government to ensure protection for OFWs in Syria and in the whole of the Middle East; and 3) for the Aquino Administration to reconsider its options in forging further military ties with the United States government, particularly in providing the US military
temporary access and deployment of troops in the
country to prevent the Philippines from being drawn in the conflict and a target of retaliatory military actions from Syria and its allies. He further stated that the US government´s planned unilateral action is
against the interests of the people of Syria and the whole of the Middle East.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.15, p.22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.
