rows.author: F081;
rows.title_full: OPPOSITION OF THE PEOPLE OF LAGUNA TO THE DETENTION OF MS. JANET NAPOLES AT THE FORT STO. DOMINGO DETENTION CENTER
rows.abstract:
Rep. Fernandez expressed his strong objection to
the use of the Cuartel de Santo Domingo in Sta.
Rosa, Laguna as a detention center by the law enforcement authorities for high profile persons. He claimed that Cuartel de Santo Domingo is one of the three declared historical sites in Sta. Rosa, Laguna and is historically valuable and significant to its people because it is in Cuartel de Santo Domingo where they trace their history and culture. He explained that with the detention at Fort Santo Domingo of Ms. Janet Lim Napoles, the alleged mastermind of the socalled “Pork Barrel Scam” and the detention in the past of even more high-profile political personages, the historical significance of Cuartel de Santo Domingo would now seem to have been eroded. He thereafter underscored that the people of Sta. Rosa would prefer that Cuartel de Santo Domingo be rather known by their people and their descendants as
a military quarters of the people of Sta. Rosa who had risked their lives for the sake of the country. He then appealed to the law enforcement authorities and the national government to put a stop to the practice of using Cuartel de Santo Domingo as a permanent detention center for high profile detainees.
(SOURCE: House Journal No.15, p. 22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G093;
rows.title_short: Remarks Of Asst. Secretary Torres Addressed To Rep. Rido During The Budget Hearing
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Tinio rose to
take exception to the apparently condescending
remarks made by Assistant Secretary Virginia Torres of the Land Transportation Office (LTO) against Rep. Terry L. Ridon who, during the Committee hearing on the budget proposal of the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) that morning, questioned Asec Torres about a video showing her allegedly playing in a casino. Rep. Tinio raised the issue of public
accountability and asked that the existing law
enjoining government personnel from entering or
playing in casinos, as well as the appropriate
sanctions and penalties for violating the same, be applied to Asec Torres.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RULES since 2013-09-02
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: H072;
rows.title_full: AERIAL STRIKE IN SAGADA, MOUNTAIN PROVINCE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ridon denounced the air strikes conducted
by the military and police forces in the four municipalities of Mountain Province in August 2013, purportedly to penetrate the camps of the New People´s Army (NPA). He pointed out that they had adversely affected food and water sources, livelihood opportunities, tourism, and human rights including the right of ancestral domain of the indigenous communities therein. As he asked that the government stop its intensified
Oplan Bayanihan campaign in the region, he urged Congress to investigate the damages that
resulted from militarization, the reasons behind the attacks, and the use of military and police funds. He also asked his colleagues to join the call for the resumption of talks between the government and the National Democratic Front; and to hear the pleas of the people of the Cordilleras.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 16, p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H077;
rows.title_full: CONDITION OF LAGUINDINGAN INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Juliette T. Uy from the Second District of Misamis Oriental lamented the deficiencies at the Laguindingan Airport in Misamis Oriental which had contributed to low traffic and flight flows and consequently, to a slowdown in business and development activities. She cited the lack of instruments and systems for landing and navigation, the unimplemented road widening
activities to and from the airport, the nonworking machines, and stringent parking policies. She asked the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines and the Department of Transportation and Communications to fast-track its installation targets for the airport
in order to protect current investments and encourage growth not only in her province but in the entire Northern Mindanao.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ACOSTA-ALBA
To the queries of Rep. Acosta-Alba, Rep. Uy (J.)
asserted that the government should immediately
address and install the needed machines and equipment in the Laguindingan Airport so it can be fully functional.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. DE JESUS
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. De Jesus informed the
Body of an ominous demolition of an informal settlement site in Road 10, Tondo, Manila that would displace thousands of families in favor of a road widening project and the privatization and modernization of the Manila North Harbor Port. As the affected families have voiced out their concern regarding their livelihood and relocation in the far-flung areas which
they have described as “death zones,” she requested for an indefinite moratorium on said demolition, implement an on-site and in-city development program, and set up livelihood programs in relocation sites.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 16, p. 10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Acosta-Alba. Referred to the appropriate Committee; Manifestation by Rep. De Jesus.

rows.author: C001;
rows.title_full: STATE OF POLITICS IN NORTHERN SAMAR
rows.abstract:
Rep. Abayon spoke on the abuse of power of a
father-and-son tandem that threatened and ravished the Province of Northern Samar which has been denied of effective representation for six long years and deprived of economic relief. He said however that while the people of Northern Samar have spoken in the last congressional election, forgetting the past is
not sine qua non to program development and pursuing justice is not anathema to reconci liation. Subsequently, Rep. Abayon traced the political career of the father-and-son tandem of Messrs. Raul and Paul Daza, who both served as Governor of Northern Samar one after the other. He claimed that it was during their time that the province retrogressed to become the poorest in the country. Then thanking President Benigno S. Aquino III for standing in the way of graft and corruption in his province and extricating
the people from poverty, he disclosed that the
President did not win overwhelmingly in Northern
Samar because of former Governor Daza´s (R.)
treacherous deal with former President Gloria Macapagal- Arroyo through some P1.5 billion worth of projects. He thereafter referred to the announcement the previous week of former Governor Daza that the latter would soon assume the position of Representative of the First District of Northern Samar because of the
commitment of the House of Representatives Electoral Tribunal (HRET) and some Liberal Party members. Rep. Abayon claimed that it was a downright attempt to tarnish the reputation of both the President and the HRET. He said that the people of Northern Samar no longer believe in the father-and-son tandem, and expressed hope that the HRET would not be swayed by such malicious misrepresentations. In behalf of his constituents, he thanked the President for campaigning for their cause and liberating them
from the Dazas, and moved for the conduct of a congressional inquiry on the plunder of the Help for Catubig Agricultural Advancement Program (HCAAP) funds.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Reps. Abayon and Dela Cruz discussed the
anomalies involved in the HCAAP and the Millennium Development Goal (MDG) projects implemented during the term of former Governor Daza (R.), as well as the latter´s attempts to influence the activities of the HRET as expressed in his speech during a recent barangay night celebration in Rep. Abayon´s district.
Rep. Abayon confirmed to Rep. Dela Cruz of his
intention to call for a congressional inquiry into the matter.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ONG
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Durano,
Rep. Emil L. Ong aired his concern about the
conviction of the Daza dynasty by the National Democratic Front for allegedly being corrupt, murderers and drug lord coddlers. He also expressed the elation of certain people for the victory of Rep. Abayon in the last congressional election. The two Members agreed that the Commission on Elections should be commended and thanked for holding an automated election in Northern Samar thus doing away with manual poll counting which was blamed for the loss of Rep. Abayon in the past two congressional elections.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 16, p. 11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Dela Cruz and Ong. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H088;
rows.title_full: METROBANK AWARDEES FOR THE COUNTRY'S OUTSTANDING POLICEMEN IN SERVICE
rows.title_short: Honoring Few Policemen And Women Who Are Recipients Of C O P S Award
rows.abstract:
Rep. Pagdilao focused on this year´s awardees of
Metrobank Foundation´s Search for the Country´s
Outstanding Policemen in Service (COPS) in
partnership with the Rotary Club of New Manila
East, the PSBank and the Philippine National Police. He said that the awardees from the police service were honored for their extra ordinary accomplishments primarily achieved through the partnership between the police and the community. He then related the origins of the COPS Award beginning in the early 1990s and his contributions to its development, which culminated in the signing of a memorandum of agreement between Metrobank Foundation, Rotary Club of New Manila East, and the PNP in 2002, which outlined the parameters for the COPS Search. After commending the presidents of Metrobank Foundation, Rotary Club of New Manila East, and PSBank for collaborating and coming up with such a prestigious award, Rep. Pagdilao then introduced and congratulated the COPS awardees who were present in the gallery.
In keeping with the tradition of honoring and
commending the COPS awardees, Rep. Pagdilao
asked that he be included as coauthor of a resolution filed by Rep. Niel C. Tupas Jr., honoring the country´s outstanding men and women in police service. He also acknowledged the presence of the country´s outstanding teachers and soldiers in the gallery.
REMARKS OF THE CHAIR
The Chair joined Rep. Pagdilao in congratulating
the awardees for their unwavering service to the
country.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 16, p.15)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2013-09-10
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Commitee.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz brought to the attention of the
Body the increasingly problematic rice situation in the country especially the spiraling costs of rice and the conflicting statements of the National Food Authority (NFA) administrator on the rice sufficiency program of the government. He stated that despite all the signs of an impending rice crisis, the NFA continues to insist that affordable rice is very much
available when the price of rice has already been
increasing at an alarming rate. He then reminded that President Benigno S. Aquino III had mandated and approved a program for rice self-sufficiency through public-private partnership that would give the private sector the much-needed incentives to ensure rice sufficiency.
He then referred to the resolution he filed urging the appropriate House Committee to look into the alleged rice import kickbacks and the implementation of the President´s Rice-Self Sufficiency Program.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ONG
Rep. Ong initially sought Rep. Dela Cruz´ views
on the 40% tax being imposed to imported rice, this as he pointed out that rice is a basic commodity and should be taxed lower than the luxury items as mandated by the Constitution. He also inquired into the public bidding procedure for smuggled rice which he claimed is usually awarded to the smugglers themselves because of their undue advantage of knowing the cost and bid price. He suggested the filing of a measure requiring all smuggled rice to be given directly to the NFA.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
Reps. Biazon and Dela Cruz exchanged views
regarding the strategies of NFA under its rice
sufficiency program, particularly on rice importation, price subsidy and inputs support to local farmers, price support to urban poor consumers, and marketing of local rice through farmers´cooperatives.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Rep. Atienza´s initial queries focused on the
issues of rice hoarding and increasing price of rice, which Rep. Dela Cruz said should be clarified by the public officials concerned in a congressional hearing. The Members also discussed the various anomalies troubling the Department of Agriculture, such as the Napoles pork barrel fiasco and the fertilizer scam. Rep. Atienza expressed hope that Congress would find ways to ferret out the truth regarding all these lost funds that should benefit the concerned sectors. Rep. Dela Cruz reiterated that he
filed a resolution urging Congress to investigate the country´s lamentable rice situation and immediately resolve the same.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAEZ
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Paez at the outset
congratulated Rep. Dela Cruz for raising the issue on the price of rice. Thereafter, they discussed the following concerns: the policy or conditions on rice importation as a regulated transaction; the regulatory body that undertakes such function; the conflicting functions of the NFA as commercial trader and regulatory body; the irregularity on rice importation from Vietnam; and the proposal to revise the NFA
charter.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 17, pp.12-13)
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2014-02-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Ong, Biazon, Atienza and Paez. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2013-11-19
Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2014-01-27
Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2014-02-04
committee_action.remarks: The Committee decided to terminate the inquiry and instructed the Committee Secretariat to prepare the committee report.

rows.author: F048;
rows.title_full: ALLEGED ANOMALIES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE HELP FOR CATUBIG PROJECT IN NORTHERN SAMAR
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ong initially explained that the basis for his legislative development program during his two previous terms as Congressman is providing basic infrastructure and agricultural develop ment projects in his congressional district to uplift his constituents from poverty, although in a limited way considering his main task of proposing legislation. It is within this context that Rep. Ong raised the implementation issues
affecting the Help Catubig Agricultural Advance ment Program (HCAAP) development project funded by a multibillion loan from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation-Official Development
Assistance (JBIC-ODA) Fund which aimed to promote
sustainable agriculture and economic development
in the Second District of Northern Samar.
Rep. Ong thereafter called for a congressional
investigation on the nonimplementation and noncompletion of the HCAAP development project and the misuse of public funds with the purpose of making erring public officials responsible for their alleged involvement in graft and corruption. He also mentioned his previous request for the Commission on Audit (COA) to investigate and submit an audit report on the HCAAP development project which to date had remained unanswered. Rep. Ong then claimed that former Rep. Raul A. Daza and former Governor Paul Daza were allegedly involved in the anomalies affecting the nonimplementation of the HCAAP project. This, as he further lamented on the unexplained wealth of the Daza family, as well as the continued reign of terror by some members of the Philippine National Police
in Northern Samar which he said is a glaring
violation of the people´s rights to peace and privacy.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 17, p.16)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-09-04)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F035;
rows.title_full: NAMRIA MAPPING
rows.title_short: Modernization Of N A M R I A
rows.abstract:
Rep. Gunigundo underscored the importance of
the completion of a new unified topographic map of the Philippines that is being undertaken by the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA) and the Certeza Infosys Corporation (CIC). He then argued why the deferment of the unified mapping program being undertaken by the NAMRIA and the CIC will seriously affect the implementation of crucial development projects. He asked that the pertinent officials of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) reconsider the issuance of a memorandum
order deferring the unified mapping program; for the Department of Science and Technology (DOST)
officials to sign a memorandum of agreement with
the NAMRIA; and for the Department of Budget and
Management (DBM) to provide budgetary alloca tions for the continuation of the unified
mapping program for the years 2014-2016. He
opined that the new unified topographical map of the Philippines will be the President´s legacy to the country.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Speaking in Filipino, Reps. Atienza and
Gunigundo discussed various concerns regarding the suspension of a contract that would complete the mapping of the Philippine islands. Rep. Atienza said he would support any action of Rep. Gunigundo to protect the integrity of government.
(SOURCE: Journal No.18, p.14)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H046;
rows.title_full: IMPLEMENTATION OF K TO 12
rows.abstract:
Rep. Olivarez delved on the problems of the
education sector in implementing the K-12 basic
education program of the Aquino Administration.
While he is a staunch ally of the K-12 program,
Rep. Olivarez pointed out the following concerns
facing the program implementors: 1) the inevi table birth pains in the program launching; 2) senior high school conundrum; and 3) the two-year college vacuum, among others. He cited figures on the forthcoming increase in enrolment in senior high school as he continued to explain why colleges and universities would eventually run out of students and why such laws as allowing college faculty to teach senior high school students and increasing government subsidies in private schools, should be passed. He then discussed the annual increase in
student enrolment as well as out-of-school youth and the decrease in student performance especially in Math and Science, as other factors that have an impact on the country´s aim of quality education that is responsive to the demands of globalization.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. TAMBUNTING
Rep. Tambunting sought clarification on the
benefits and funding requirement of the new educational system. Rep. Olivarez, in response, mentioned the three target areas of the academic, technical and vocational education, and the sports and science education; shared his colleague´s support for Rep. Biazon´s proposal to channel PDAF funds to the Department of Education (DepEd); and agreed that a resolution should be filed on transition measures from the basic education system to the K-12 system.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
Rep. Biazon discussed with Rep. Olivarez the
problems arising in the increase in enrolment for
Grade 11 in 2016 as a result of the implementa tion of the K-12 system. Both Members also discussed the additional allocation needed for the implementation of the K-12 program, with Rep. Biazon stating that Congress should inquire into the matter and request the DepEd to make an in-depth examination of the program. He also proposed the realignment of the 2014 budget of the PDAF to the DepEd to address the consequent shortages of classrooms and teachers brought about by the implementation of the K-12 program.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 18, pp.14-15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Tambunting and Biazon. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G057;
rows.title_full: ATROCITIES BY THE MNLF IN ZAMBOANGA CITY
rows.abstract:
As he appealed for the support of his colleagues
for a lasting and meaningful peace in Mindanao, Rep. Loong spoke on the Bangsamoro independence and freedom from the Republic of the Philippines
declared by Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF)
Chairperson Nur Misuari after being notified by the Organization of Islamic Conference (OIC) of the intent of the Philippine government to terminate the six-year review of the 1996 GRP-MNLF Final Peace Agreement. He informed the Body that early that morning, MNLF forces attacked the City of Zamboanga and engaged the government forces in a gun battle. He said that local leaders like him are deeply disturbed and worried that the incident might worsen, leading to the destruction of properties and loss of lives. Given the prevailing deteriorating peace and order situation in Mindanao, Rep. Loong suggested that the Philippine government must: 1) device a comprehensive peace process concerning all Muslim rebel forces; 2) reconcile all its agreements with the rebel forces so as to bring unity and understanding among the Muslim rebel groups; 3) implement its agreement and commitment to the Muslim rebel forces, including the 1996 Final Peace Agreement
with the MNLF; and 4) pursue the finalization of the Bangsamoro Framework Agreement with the Moro
Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) without
disregarding the Organic Act for the Autonomous
Region in Muslim Mindanao and the 1996 Final
Peace Agreement. Finally, he called on his Muslim
brothers in various government and private sectors to support the peace process, and asked the rebels to unite their efforts as one people through peaceful means.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
After briefly discussing the government´s peace
efforts in Mindanao including his previous proposals thereon, Rep. Biazon tackled with Rep. Loong the steps being taken by the police and military forces to promote the rule of law in the country and prevent that morning´s MNLF attack against government forces in Zamboanga City from turning into a worse situation. They also discussed the need to unite the three factions now comprising the MNLF and the possible ways to do it, as well as the urgency to
conduct a congressional inquiry into the recent
MNLF incident.
(SOURCE: Journal No.18, p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Biazon. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H080;
rows.title_short: Congress Is Not The Center Of Gravity Of Massive Graft And Corruption
rows.abstract:
Rep. Señeres initially congratulated his fellow
Mindanaoan, Deputy Speaker Balindong for his
election as Deputy Speaker from Mindanao. He then
delivered a speech to rebut the allegation that
Congress is the epicenter of massive graft and
corruption in the country by raising the following points, among others: 1) the World Bank estimates that about 30 percent or about P500 billion of the annual budget goes to graft and corruption; and 2) the budget for Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF), if truly being wasted to massive graft and corruption, comprises just a miniscule three percent
of the amount being announced by the World Bank.
He added that the Office of the Ombudsman and
the Commission on Audit should have responded to
the allegation of the international agency by asking them the specific bases of its estimate. He thereafter commended the neophyte Members of the House for initiating efforts to stop graft and corruption, particularly for opposing the PDAF and heeding public opinion.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PADILLA
After commending the anti-corruption efforts of
the neophyte solons, Rep. Padilla mentioned that the House leadership under the Speaker and himself included, had also endorsed the decision of the President to abolish the PDAF. He then used the more conservative estimate of the Philippine Anti- Graft Commission that only 20 percent of the national budget is lost to graft and corruption every year, to illustrate that the PDAF constitutes a measly 1.4 percent of the 2013 national budget. Reps. Padilla and Señeres agreed on the need to institute reforms in public spending and to prosecute and convict corrupt officials in all branches of government. The former however pointed out that there may also be more anomalies made by other government agencies which are worthy of greater attention than the public scrutiny of the lawmakers´ PDAF.
(SOURCE: Jounal No. 19, p.9)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-09-10)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Padilla. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H002;
rows.title_full: TRIBUTE TO PRESIDENT OSMENA
rows.abstract:
Rep. Abellanosa paid homage to Sergio Osmeña
Sr., who is considered to be the pride of the
Cebuanos. In behalf of all the Representatives of
Cebu, as well as all the other Members there from, he thanked Senior Sto. Niño for giving them the former President. As the country remembers the birth anniversary of President Osmeña, Rep. Abellanosa enjoined his colleagues to continue the fight against poverty and corruption so that the people will enjoy the independence that the nation´s forefathers fought
hard for.
(SOURCE: Journal No.19,p.9)
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G057;
rows.title_full: UNIMPLEMENTED PROVISIONS OF THE ORGANIC ACT FOR AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
rows.title_short: Unimplemented Provisions Of The A R M M
rows.abstract:
MANIFESTATION OF REP. LOONG
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Gullas,
Rep. Tupay T. Loong manifested, for incorporation
into the privilege speech that he delivered the
previous day, that the unimplemented provisions of Republic Act (RA) 9054 or the Organic Act for the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM)
have caused the Moro National Liberation Front to
believe that it is being ignored by the national government thus causing the group to continue its struggle. He cited in particular the failure by the government to implement certain provisions of RA 9054 in compliance with the 1996 Final Peace Agreement including, among others, the ARMM representation in central government or national government departments
and offices by election or appointment;
membership in the Executive department, constitutional bodies, National Security Council, and government corporations; appointment of qualified ARMM jurists in the Judiciary and to the Judicial and Bar Council; creation of the Office of the Deputy Court Administrator for the ARMM; and the provisions
promoting fiscal autonomy in the region.
(SOURCE: Journal No.19, p.10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.title_full: \"RUGGIE FRAMEWORK\" FOR HUMAN RIGHTS AND BUSINESS RIGHTS
rows.title_short: Human Rights Violations Relative To Mining In Nueva Vizcaya
rows.abstract:
Rep. Padilla spoke about the mining operations
in the Province of Nueva Vizcaya and the human
rights violations besetting the same. Discussing the issue within the context of the Ruggie framework on business and human rights, he revealed the human rights violations being committed by Oceana Gold, Royalco Resources Ltd. and FCF mining companies to the indigenous peoples (IPs) of Nueva Vizcaya, and the firms´ nonpayment of proper excise taxes. He then recommended: 1) the immediate deportation of Oceana Gold´s general manager for acts proved to be inimical to the people of Didipio and for the punishment of the security guards involved therein; 2) the strict implementation of
Section 59 of the Indigenous Peoples Rights Act
(IPRA), pending the enactment of a new law and the compliance by mining companies with the
requirements of free and prior informed consent
before any mining operation is allowed; 3) the
President´s adoption of the recommendation of the
Commission on Human Rights to terminate Oceana
Gold´s financial or technical assistance agreement (FTAA); 4) the Bureau of Internal Revenue´s investigation of Oceana Gold for violations of the Internal Revenue Code; 5) the immediate cancellation of the 10-year explora tion permit of Royalco Resources Ltd.; and 6) the immediate implementation of the provisions of Executive Order No. 79 on responsible mining.
(JOURNAL NO.19,p.20)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F060;
rows.title_full: BARRICADE OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN A MINING COMPANY IN CLAVER, SURIGAO DEL NORTE
rows.title_short: Controversies Over Mining Operations In Surigao Del Norte
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Gerald Anthony V. Gullas Jr.,
the Chair recognized Rep. Guillermo A. Romarate Jr. from the Second District of Surigao del Norte who spoke about a standoff between a group of Manobo tribesmen demanding mining royalty payments from ADNAMA Mining Resources Inc. for their mining activities in certain areas of Claver, Surigao del Norte which they claimed are part of their ancestral domain. He thereafter called on the Committee on National Cultural Communities to immediately conduct an investiga tion in aid of legislation into the matter to establish if the royalty demands and the
claimants are legitimate, and if the apparent
intervention of certain local government officials by encouraging false claims and acts of extortion, are within the purview of the law.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BAG-AO
Rep. Bag-ao inquired into the status of the investigation conducted by the previous Congress regarding the claim of the Manobos on the revenues from the mining operations of the ADNAMA Mining Resources, Inc., in Surigao del Norte. She expressed her support to the call of Rep. Romarate for another congressional investigation by the Committee on National
Cultural Communities on the particular concern
which she pointed out has been brought before
the local government of Dinagat Islands. She said
that it is likewise the concern of other indigenous communities in the Caraga region.
(SOURCE: Journal No.19, p.20-21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Bag-ao. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_full: LACK OF EFFECTIVE GOVERNANCE IN METRO MANILA
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza adverted to the issue of yesterday´s
flooding in Metro Manila to call attention to a
perennial concern and the absence of government´s
response during a time of calamity. He claimed that the heavy flooding had brought the govern ment again to a “nonreactive” state and called to task the traffic enforcers from the Metro Manila Development Authority (MMDA) for their absence in the streets of the metropolis to provide solutions to the ensuing chaos and traffic congestion. Considering the adverse
effects of instant flooding, traffic congestion, and peace and order problems in the metropolis, he argued for the creation of the position of a Metro Manila governor and the creation of a Metro Manila government that will address the aforecited perennial concerns, including the lack of public accountability of government officials to the residents of Metro Manila.
Rep. Atienza informed the Body that he will file
the requisite measure that will address the concerns of Metro Manila residents. He also expressed the hope that President Benigno S. Aquino III would take action on these concerns.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ERICE
Rep. Erice stated that being a former employee
of the defunct Metro Manila Commission, he had
already witnessed the perennial problems of Metro
Manila. He however admitted to being aware of the
sacrifices that the present MMDA chair is doing to come up with a solution to the gargantuan problems that the MMDA is facing. He averred that with so much responsibility, the MMDA is lacking in authority and resources and instead of being criticized, the agency should be given the proper funding and authority to be able to fulfill its responsibilities.
(SOURCE: Journal No.19, p.21)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on METRO MANILA DEVELOPMENT since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Erice. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G095;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Umali delved into a truthful assessment of
how far the promised reforms of the Electric Power
Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) of 2001 have gone and
how much benefits and returns have been realized
from investments in the reformed and restructured
power industry. He stated that when the EPIRA was passed in the 11th Congress, it was widely taunted as the solution to the chronic shortages in power supply and the answer to the unstable and high power rates. Unfortunately, he lamented that the objectives of the EPIRA have not been attained as the power landscape is littered with rulings, orders, decisions and administrative issuances of the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) that would fall short of the promise to protect and promote consumer interest. Furthermore, he added that there are sectors in the power industry that are undergoing unbundling and restructuring of their generation, transmission, distribution and supply systems resulting to power rate increases and frequent brownouts in Mindoro and Mindanao. With the EPIRA falling short of its promise for a
stable and reliable power supply at a reasonable
price, Rep. Umali urged his colleagues to revisit and immediately review the EPIRA as Congress has to enact policies that would genuinely address the
concerns of the energy sector.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. MASONGSONG
Rep. Masongsong discussed with Rep. Umali
(R.) the need to amend certain provisions of the
EPIRA because of its failure to: 1) fully address the huge debt of the power industry; 2) entice the private sector to join in the business of power generation; and 3) enable the Department of Energy to perform its task of managing power plants and providing proper business environment in the power sector. He thereafter expressed his support to the proposal of reviewing and amending the EPIRA.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. ATIENZA
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Atienza´s queries
focused on the increasing rate of electricity in the country as compared to other nations, given the fact that the Malampaya Fund is adequate enough to subsidize power cost or develop energy resources. He thereafter expressed hope that said fund would be properly used even by the next administration to address the country´s power requirements, and suggested a study on the use of coal-powered plants to lower the cost of electricity. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RIDON
Rep. Ridon discussed with Rep. Umali (R.)certain issues regarding the need for a comprehensive
review of the EPIRA to attain the law´s objective of generating lower and reasonable power rates which they agreed would result in the protection and benefit of power consumers and industries and make the economy more globally competitive. They also tackled the benefits that would redound to the public with the broadening of the ownership base of power generation companies, the fair and nondiscriminatory treatment of public and private sector entities in the process of restructuring the power industry and the creation of an independent regulatory body.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Rodolfo G.
Biazon´s questions focused on two major issues
which are the concerns of the resolutions that he had filed before the House: 1) the urgency of reviewing the EPIRA; and 2) the exploration of other energy sources, specifically coal which is being hampered by concerns on climate change, the prior consent of the affected communities, and food security. Rep. Umali (R.) assured his colleague that the Committee on Energy which he heads will prioritize the review of the EPIRA and that Rep. Biazon´s second concern will be given preference in the agenda of the Committee´s next hearings. 
INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAGDILAO
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Gullas, Reps. Samuel D. Pagdilao and Umali (R.)
discussed the reasons behind the need to review and amend certain provisions of the EPIRA; the
possibility of reverting to the old system of
monopoly as a means to lower the cost of energy;
and the utilization of the Malampaya Fund to support the energy requirements of the country.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOONG
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep.
Abaya, Rep. Tupay T. Loong exchanged views with
Rep. Umali (R.) regarding the possibility of bringing down electricity rates in the Philippines even if it is not an oil-producing country. They also talked about the issue of the location abroad of the headquarters of foreign oil explorers doing business in the country. 
(SOURCE: House Journal No.21, pp.21-23)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Masongsong, Atienza, Ridon, Biazon, Pagdilao and Loong. Referred to the appropriate Commitee.

rows.author: G093;
rows.title_full: CONDEMNED THE ARREST OF ANAKPAWIS PARTY-LIST REPRESENTATIVE HICAP AT HACIENDA LUISITA
rows.title_short: Arrest Of Rep. Hicap In Hacienda Luisita
rows.abstract:
Rep. Tinio rose to condemn the arrest made by
Tarlac City Philippine National Police (PNP) of their colleague from Party-List Anakpawis, Rep. Fernando “Ka Pando” L. Hicap, together with the other members of the fact-finding team looking into the human rights violations in Hacienda Luisita, while conducting a protest action therein. He stressed that their arrest is illegal as it violates their right to assembly and free expression, and to conduct an independent inquiry into human rights violations in a ranch owned by the President´s family. As such, he called on the House to investigate the matter and join him in demanding for the immediate release of Rep. Hicap and his companions.
(Source: JOURNAL NO. 21,p.9)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.title_full: BUGKALOT TRIBE'S RIGHTFUL SHARE FROM THE PROCEEDS OF THE CASECNAN MULTI-PURPOSE IRRIGATION PROJECT
rows.title_short: Rights And Benefits Of Bugkalot Tribe In The Casecnan Dam Operations
rows.abstract:
Rep. Padilla dwelled on the contents of a letter
addressed to President Benigno S. Aquino III from
the mayor of Nagtipunan, Quirino Province, who is
also the overall chieftain of the Bugkalot or Ilongot Tribe from the indigenous cultural communities (ICCs) of Nueva Vizcaya, Quirino and Aurora. He then read into the Record of the House several portions of the letter which dealt with the problems being encountered by the Bugkalot ICCs in their ancestral domain where the CE Casecnan Water and Energy Company, Inc. is operating and maintaining a diversion dam.
He then discussed in particular the refusal of CE
Casecnan to honor a provision in the Indigenous
People´s Rights Act (IPRA) which gives ICCs the
right to benefit and to share the profits from the allocation and utilization of natural resources within their ancestral domain. Because of the patent display of ungratefulness of CE Casecnan, Rep. Padilla underscored that the Bugkalot tribe has decided to exercise their rights under Section 7 of the IPRA by convening
the soonest time in Nueva Vizcaya to do some
cultural practices and rituals and discuss ways of regulating the entry of CE Casecnan into their domain. In closing his speech, Rep. Padilla asked that the letter be made the basis of any congressional inquiry that will be conducted regarding the matter at the proper time.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Initially, Rep. Dela Cruz gave his full support to the demand of the Bugkalot tribe because they deserve to have their three percent royalty share in allowing CE Casecnan to enter and utilize their ancestral domain. He thereafter inquired on the amount that the CE Casecnan has been generating. The Sponsor pointed out that the Bugkalots had received nothing and their fishing activities had even suffered from pollution. Rep. Dela Cruz expressed dismay, saying the IPRA and the host community law
protect multi-purpose dams which serve the national interest and development. Rep. Dela Cruz expressed hope that the dispute will be settled amicably and to the satisfaction of the
Bugkalot tribe.
(Source: HOUSE JOURNAL NO.21,pp.5-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: SOUGHT CLARIFICATION ON THE GUIDELINES OF THE HOUSE REGARDING THE REFUSAL OF ENTRY TO VISITORS WHO WISH TO OBSERVE PLENARY PROCEEDINGS
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. De Jesus brought to
the attention of the Body an incident involving a
group of health advocates who were refused entry
into the Session Hall to listen to the 2014 GAB debates, particularly on the proposed budget of the Department of Health (DOH). She stated that she, together with Reps. Ilagan and Zarate, had forwarded their concern to the Legislative Security Bureau, per advice of the Secretary General, but were given the run-around. Thereupon, Rep. De Jesus registered her protest
to the said incident and called upon the leadership of the House to define the policy and process of accepting guests in the Session Hall as well as to investigate the matter and make sure that those responsible would be held accountable.
(Source: HOUSE JOURNAL NO.21,p.113)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee. Referred to the Office of the Sergeant-At-Arms on 2013-10-23

rows.author: H056;
rows.title_full: DEVASTATION CAUSED BY TYPHOON \"SANTI\" TO THE PROVINCE OF NUEVA ECIJA
rows.title_short: Effects Of Typhoon \" Santi \" In Nueva Ecija
rows.abstract:
Rep. Suansing informed the Body of the damage
wrought by Typhoon “Santi” to property, infrastructure, and agriculture in the Province of Nueva Ecija, which left many of her constituents hungry, homeless and helpless. She appealed to the Executive Department to allocate the necessary funds for the required rehabilitation of Nueva Ecija and said that she will file the corresponding resolution on this request, if necessary.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. BIAZON
As chairperson of the House Panel of the Congressional Oversight Committee on Disaster Risk Reduction, Rep. Biazon inquired whether Rep. Suansing would answer clarificatory questions.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. BIAZON
After initially disclosing that the members of the House panel of the Congressional Oversight Committee on Disaster Risk Reduction have yet to be designated, Rep. Biazon discussed with Rep. Suansing the estimated budget needed for agricultural rehabilitation, infrastructure reconstruction and economic recovery in Nueva Ecija, with the latter explaining that an evaluation of the extent of the damages in the
province was still ongoing. Rep. Biazon thereafter maintained that the President
could provide the required budgetary funding to
address the calamity situation in Nueva Ecija and
other provinces in the affected regions considering that the Executive Department had provided for the immediate release of funds to address various calamities in the past, as in the case of Zamboanga City which recently received billions of pesos in calamity
assistance. He also inquired whether the local government units in Nueva Ecija had earmarked a portion of their income as calamity funds, as mandated by law.
Rep. Suansing then explained that although the
LGUs initially responded to the crisis, their resources
were inadequate. She agreed with Rep. Biazon that
the Representatives of the other affected provinces
should coauthor a Resolution on the matter.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. ANTONINO-NADRES
On motion of Rep. Gunigundo, the Chair recognized
Rep. Magnolia Rosa C. Antonino-Nadres who
described the destruction also caused by Typhoon
“Santi” in her district. She joined the call for the Executive Branch to address the needs of their constituents. 
(SOURCE: Journal No.22, pp.24-25)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Biazon; Manifestation by Rep. Antonino-Nadres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: C128;
rows.title_full: STATE OF COOPERATIVES
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. PAEZ
Citing the worldwide celebration of Cooperative
Month, Rep. Paez stressed that the cooperative sector in the Philippines aims to address socio-economic inequality by making cooperatives financially viable, stable, and responsive to the needs of its members. As he discussed the continuing growth of cooperatives in terms of membership, assets, employment generation, geographical presence, volume of business
and governance, Rep. Paez stated that the cooperative sector has taken millions out of poverty, developed leadership potential among the grassroots, empowered the poor with trainings on cooperative governance and technical expertise, helped build better
communities, and recorded several milestones,
such as the establishment of the Standard Chart of Account for Cooperatives and the passage of the Philippine Cooperative Code of 2008, among others. In conclusion, Rep. Paez urged his colleagues to support the following key legislative agenda which the cooperative sector hopes to realize in the 16th Congress: 1) amendment of the CDA Charter in order
to strengthen its supervisory and regulatory powers; 2) passage of the Agrarian and Agricultural Credit Consolidation measure which will benefit farmers, fisherfolks and agrarian-based organizations; 3) amendment to the National Electrification Administration
Charter; 4) passage of a bill creating a Water
Regulatory Commission; and 5) establishment of a
Microfinance Code of the Philippines, among others.
(SOURCE: Journal No.22,p.26)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: H066;
rows.title_full: COOPERATIVES AND NGOs
rows.title_short: Cooperatives Tarnished By Pork Barrel Scam
rows.abstract:
PRIVILEGE SPEECH OF REP. BRAVO (A.)
As the country celebrates the National Cooperative Month, Rep. Bravo took the floor to defend cooperatives and other civil society organizations (CSOs) whose noble work has been tarnished because of the pork barrel scam involving fake nongovernment organizations (NGOs). He stressed the mandate and definition of cooperatives pursuant to Republic
Act (RA) No. 9520 or the Philippine Cooperative
Code of 2008 and described their unique identity
as well as their significant role in promoting peoplecentered development and the principles of accountability and transparency. Calling on the government and the public to recognize cooperatives as a powerful tool for social empowerment, Rep. Bravo cited the need to strengthen them and ensure their viability. He urged the government to create an atmosphere conducive to the development of cooperatives through effective regulation and access to support services.
(SOURCE: Journal No.22,p.26)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H044;
rows.title_full: ZAMBOANGA CRISIS
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Lilia Macrohon-Nuño ...spoke about the
search for lasting peace in Mindanao especially in Zamboanga City which was recently ravaged by war. She narrated how the month-long bloody fighting between the government military and police forces and the members of a faction of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) began and ended, resulting to loss of human lives, damage to property, trauma to her constituents, and economic havoc in Zamboanga City. She condemned the injustice done to the people
of Zamboanga by the MNLF and demanded justice
and retribution in their behalf. This, as she wondered why Mr. Nur Misuari of the MNLF chose Zamboanga City as the staging point to ventilate his grievances against the ongoing peace talks between the government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) when the city is not even part of the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) or the envisioned Bangsamoro Region. She then urged the Body to assist in the reconstruction of Zamboanga City and, together with Rep. Celso L. Lobregat, thanked her colleagues and other people and organizations for their generous donations to fast track the relief and rehabilitation operations in the city. She also thanked the President and other key government officials for their personal
attention to resolve the Zamboanga crisis. She then implored Congress to make the quest for peace in Mindanao a top priority, which she opined could only be achieved if poverty, lack of livelihood and educational opportunities, and inadequate health facilities and social services are addressed in the region.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES
Rep Señeres averred that the war could have
been prevented if not for the inadequacy and incompetence on the part of pertinent government officials to infuse the right kind of ingredients into the peace process. Relating his participation in the government´s peace initiatives with the MNLF during the Ramos Administration, he however noted that there
will be no complete peace settlement in Mindanao if the government will not involve both the MNLF and the MILF in the peace process.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. SEÑERES (Continuation)
To Rep. Señeres´ query as to whether the socalled
peace talks led by the Office of the Presidential
Adviser on the Peace Process (OPAPP) lack the
proper ingredients that would end the rebellion in Mindanao, Rep. Macrohon-Nuño agreed with said
statement but stressed that her speech was more concerned with the atrocities done by Mr. Misuari´s group to the people of Zamboanga City which is not part of the ARMM.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 22,pp.26-27)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-10-23
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Seneres. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F100;
rows.abstract:
... Rep. Neri J. Colmenares of Party-List Bayan Muna spoke about the unconstitutional and unlawful issuance by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) in July 2012 of National Budget Circular (NBC) No. 541 wherein the President had ordered the withdrawal of all unobligated allotments of all agencies with low-level of obligations as of June 30, 2012 for both continuing and current allotments. He pointed out that the funds were realigned and pooled under the Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP)which he described as the latest and worst form of presidential pork barrel. Rep. Colmenares explained that the President´s reference to the Constitution,the Administrative Code and the General Appropriations Act (GAA) of 2012 or RA No. 10155 as the legal justifications for the DAP, does not legitimize the program per se as it fails to support the requirements and definitions of the term “savings” under the 2012 GAA which particularly requires congressional approval on all matters concerning appropriation of public funds including savings. He further explained that even the President´s use of the impoundment provision in the GAA cannot be used as a legal basis for the DAP to realign funds considering that this subverts the constitutional
role of Congress as the approving authority
of the budget. He thereafter proposed the abolition of the impoundment provision in the proposed 2014 GAA during its consideration on Third Reading to ensure that Congress retains its power over the purse and prevents the use of presidential pork barrel as a source of graft and corruption and patronage politics.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. TINIO
Rep. Tinio stressed at the outset that Congress
had the power of the purse. He adverted to a DBM
document stating that funds used for programs and
projects identified through DAP were sourced from
government savings. He cited the Constitution and
several laws which defined savings as unused funds from incomplete or nonimplemented projects or fund balances that were achieved as a result of efficiency; provided that funds spent from the treasury must be by appropriation of law; and prohibited the impoundment of appropriations.
Rep. Colmenares agreed that what was referred
to as savings were actually underspent agency funds withdrawn in the middle of the fiscal year and agencies which were not able to complete their projects could not be called efficient. He shared the view that the Executive rescinded agency appropriations despite the absence of a national government deficit. He and his colleague concluded that the DAP had no
constitutional and legal basis and was a form of
“presidential pork.” The Members thereafter debated on the provisions of the 2012 GAA particularly Section 54 on savings and augmentation and Sections 64 and 65 on
prohibition against impoundment of appropriations
which they agreed were violated by the President
through the DBM´s issuance of NBC No. 541 in the
implementation of the DAP. This, as Rep. Tinio
stressed Congress´ mandate of ensuring the proper
implementation of the national budget. They also discussed the P475 million DAP that was given to the Senators and was transferred to the National Livelihood Development Corporation which in turn partnered with the bogus NGOs identified with Ms. Janet Napoles. Rep. Tinio added the case of the P900-million allotment from the Malampaya Fund under the Arroyo Administration which was similarly coursed through Ms. Napoles´ NGOs.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. TINIO
Finally, Rep. Tinio inquired on the possibility of filing a plunder case against President Benigno S. Aquino III, just like the plunder case filed against former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo in connection with her alleged anomalous use of the P900- million Malampaya Fund allocation. After agreeing with the observation of Rep. Tinio, Rep. Colmenares suggested that the Body insert a provision in the proposed 2014 GAA stating that the President may only impound budgetary funds upon the approval of Congress.
(SOURCE: Journal No.22,pp.29,33&34)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-10-14)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Tinio. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_short: Disbursement Acceleration Fund ( D A F )
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. from Party-List Buhay talked about the issue of the Disbursement Acceleration Program or DAP which he said is an illegal use of public funds and is being used to destroy the very foundation of Congress. He expressed his disappointment with Budget Secretary Florencio B. Abad´s alleged misuse of public funds and appealed to his fellow Representatives and to the President to undertake the necessary measures to reform
the budgeting system.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
... Rep. Jonathan A. Dela Cruz discussed with Rep. Atienza how Budget Secretary Abad used the DAP funds to expedite the approval of the Reproductive Health (RH) Bill in the House. Their debate also dealt with the question of whether the President was misled by his subordinates with regard to his presidential powers and Congress´ exclusive power of the purse, as well as with Rep. Atienza´s proposed amendments to the 2014 General Appropriations Bill (GAB) and clarification into the DBM guidelines governing the disbursement of public funds. (SOURCE: Journal No.22,pp,34-35)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-10-14)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Dela Cruz. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F122;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Dela Cruz rose to speak on the occasion of
World Teachers´ Day. He joined the United Nations
Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
(UNESCO) and the global community in honoring
and praising teachers everywhere for their unselfish contributions in making the world a better place to live in. While he appreciated the honors given by the Department of Education and the Commission on Higher Education in coordination with Metrobank and Bato Balani Foundations to the nation´s model teachers, he urged the Members to review the compensation
packages not just for public school teachers
but from the private sector as well; and to offer
incentives so that they may become real enablers of the youth without the burdens associated with the challenges of daily life. With the hope that the Members will learn lessons from all the issues besetting the nation, such as the DAP, PDAF and Zamboanga crisis, Rep. Dela Cruz ended his speech by reading into the records three short prayers as a fitting tribute to all teachers. (SOURCE: Journal No.22,p.35)
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2013-10-14)
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: C032;
rows.title_full: PURSUE INCLUSIVE GOVERNANCE: PROTECT CHILDREN'S RIGHTS TODAY AND TOMORROW
rows.abstract:
In celebration of the National Children´s Month,
Rep. Enerio-Cerilles stressed the tradition of the House Committee on Welfare of Children, together with the Child Rights Network, of celebrating the event by sharing to the Members their views and advocacies on the rights of the child, and stressed the Committee´s theme of pursuing inclusive governance by protecting the chid´s right to participation. She averred that the Philippines must act in compliance with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of
the Child to recognize the right of children for freedom of expression along with their other rights, and entail their participation and influence in the decision and policy-making processes by heeding their voices and views on legislations concerning them. Rep. Enerio-Cerilles then thanked the Members of the 15th Congress for enacting Republic Act (RA)
No. 10165 or the Foster Care Act which envisions to lessen, if not eradicate, the number of street children. She also expressed gratitude and appreciation to the partner agencies in the Child Rights Network for their unending support and advocacy to promote the best interest of the Filipino child.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 23,p.1)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WELFARE OF CHILDREN since 2013-11-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G105;
rows.title_full: THE SITUATION OF FILIPINO CHILDREN TODAY
rows.abstract:
Speaking in Filipino, also in commemoration of
the National Children´s Month, Rep. De Jesus focused on certain issues affecting the Filipino child, including among others: the challenges and problems in the fight for children´s protection, rights and welfare; the lack of specific policies that would safeguard
the children against poverty, forced labor,
criminal syndicates and natural and man-made calamities; the absence of healthy environment and proper nutrition; the insufficient fund allocation for health services of Filipinos and for the Department of Health (DOH)-retained hospitals; and the possible eviction of the Philippine Children´s Medical Center (PCMC) from its present location by the National Housing Authority (NHA). Stressing that the bulk of the national budget should be directly allocated to address the health needs of the children, she then urged for the immediate review of the devolution of health services. She disclosed that she had filed House Resolution No. 298 seeking to rechannel the Priority Development
Assistance Fund (PDAF) of the Members to social
services, wage increases and other priority needs of the people, as well as House Resolution No. 332, calling for a comprehensive study on the importance of and other alternative programs to CCT.

INTERPELLATION OF REP. PAQUIZ
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized
Rep. Paquiz who discussed with Rep. De Jesus
her following concerns: the importance of quality
healthcare for children especially during their formal education years; the promotion of healthcare and prevention of illnesses; and the implementation of the Department of Education (DepEd) School Health Nursing Program. Rep. De Jesus committed to call the attention of the Department of Health (DOH) and other agencies
to provide more budget for the delivery of health services to public schools and hospitals while Rep. Paquiz asked the Members to help support the nurses through proper legislation on providing the right jobs and salaries to prevent the exploitation of nurses and health workers.
(SOURCE: Journal No.23,pp.1-2.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WELFARE OF CHILDREN since 2013-11-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G077;
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Noel, the Chair recognized
Rep. Rene L. Relampagos from the First District of Bohol who spoke about the 7.2-magnitude earthquake that hit Bohol and Cebu last October 15, 2013. After stating why Bohol has become a top tourist destination due to its various man-made and natural wonders, famous Boholanos and six heritage churches, four of which stand in his district, Rep. Relampagos thereafter described the extent of damages caused by the earthquake to the province, especially to his district, in terms of infrastructure and
human casualties and injuries. He said that initial government data estimated the damage to Bohol infrastructure costing billions of pesos.
Even as he mentioned the blessings which the
Boholanos still have to be thankful for despite the disaster, Rep. Relampagos urged Congress to be the guardian of culture and heritage and to ensure that disaster preparedness and risk reduction is given highest priority in every barangay. Specifically, he requested, among others: 1) the formulation of a Bohol
Recovery Program, the creation of a Bohol Rehabilitation Fund to be included in the 2014 General Appropriations Act (GAA), and the passing of a joint resolution to allow the realignment of available or unused funds in the 2013 GAA to be allocated to Bohol and other provinces affected by natural disasters, like Typhoon “Santi”; 2) the mandatory restoration
and retrofitting of all historical and cultural sites left in the country; 3) the modernization of the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Philvolcs) for the purpose of updating the current Philippine geohazard map; 4) the mandatory allocation of free freight for medical supplies and relief goods of all
aircrafts and shipping vessels; and 5) the review of guidelines on the use of calamity funds as far as disaster preparedness is concerned. In ending, he underscored that the earthquake that rocked Bohol only strengthened the people´s faith in God even more, made them count their blessings, and united their province and the whole nation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. DEL MAR
While Rep. Del Mar detailed how Cebu also suffered from the earthquake, he stressed that Bohol bore the brunt of it. Rep. Relampagos affirmed that the extent of destruction, death, injury and trauma and the cost of repair and rehabilitation in his province were worse
that what had been initially estimated and would
even worsen with the continuing aftershocks. He
stressed the need for more assistance; welcomed the postponement of barangay election in the province so as to focus on the current crisis; and thanked his colleague for suggesting that Bohol´s needs should take priority over those of Cebu´s.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 23,pp.7&8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2013-10-21
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Del Mar. Manifestation by Rep. Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G064;
rows.title_full: EFFECTS OF THE ABOLITION OF THE PDAF
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair, Rep. Nograles clarified
that he took the floor not to defend the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) but to give a eulogy on the same considering that it would no longer be incorporated in the proposed 2014 General Appropriations Act or GAA and that the Supreme court would soon issue a ruling on its legality. As he discussed the surveys conducted by Pulse Asia Research showing that majority of the people still found the PDAF useful and beneficial in serving the needs of the citizenry, Rep. Nograles pointed out that the effects of the PDAF are even more pronounced
in Mindanao as almost two-thirds of Mindanaoans
favor its retention as they view the PDAF as an equalizer considering that Mindanao always
gets the last priority in terms of government spending. Furthermore, he stated that the PDAF has augmented and supported the projects and programs that were needed to address the problems in their districts and the concerns of their constituencies. In conclusion, Rep. Nograles requested his colleagues to remember the PDAF not on its highly publicized alleged misuse but for all the benefits it has provided to many poor families, the countless scholars
who were able to finish their education, the multitude of patients who were given medicines, the many lives it helped save, the grieving families it comforted, and the hungry mouths it helped fed.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz then sought recognition from the
Chair.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Defensor, Rep. Dela Cruz said that he wanted to ask Rep. Nograles whether he believes that the statistics given by Pulse Asia is accurate or has been merely misused, this as he further asked whether under the 2014 national budget, it would now be left to the Departments concerned to give the funds for scholarship, medical assistance or infrastructure programs and projects as the case may be instead of allowing
the Members to participate in said undertakings
through their PDAF allocations. He also inquired
how the Members could approve the proposed
budget measure when they do not know what would
happen to the beneficiaries of their PDAFs, or the arrangements that would be available for their districts. He stressed that the foregoing were some of the questions that he would have posed to Rep. Nograles but who opted not to yield to interpellations.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. ATIENZA
At the outset, Rep. Atienza enjoined everyone to
commiserate with the Boholanos, the families who
lost their loved ones and the victims of the recent earthquake that hit Bohol. Being an adopted son of the province, Rep. Atienza expressed grief for the thousands of families who were displaced and therefore urgently need shelter as well as food, clean water and medicines. He disclosed that in support to the
challenge made by Rep. Del Mar to collectively help the people of Bohol, every Member of the Minority and Independent blocs would donate P10,000 each out of their own pockets. While urging everyone to not just depend on what the Executive department could do and could
not do in terms of calamity fund allocation, Rep.
Atienza urged the Members to set aside differences, to know and do their responsibilities as Members of the House, and to make a collective effort in helping the needy and suffering people of Bohol.
(SOURCE: Journal No.23,pp.9&10)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-11-20
rows.remarks: Manifestations by Reps. Dela Cruz and Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F102;
rows.title_full: WORLD FOOD DAY CELEBRATION
rows.abstract:
In celebration of the World Food Day and Farmers´
Week, Rep. Bello spoke about the reasons why
genetically modified organisms (GMOs) are controversial as they are relevant; the dangers and risks posed by GMOs which compelled many countries to have them banned; and why the Court of Appeals granted a Writ of Kalikasan that stopped field trials on Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) talong or eggplant. In the interest of consumer welfare, public health, and ecological stability, Rep. Bello proposed a moratorium on granting licenses for the import of GMO foods and crops for sale or for field testing until a viable risk assessment agency under the Department of Agriculture (DA) is created, and a ban is imposed on all field testing of all GMO crops to prevent genetic contamination.
MANIFESTATION OF REP. DELA CRUZ
Rep. Dela Cruz lamented that Rep. Bello (W.)
would not yield to a few questions considering that he has a number of issues that he would have wanted to discuss with him such as the advantages and disadvantages of genetically engineered products; the kind of frameworks, regiments and arrangements the latter is proposing; the kind of products that are already
genetically engineered in the market, still organically produced and foremost being used. He also would like to ask what steps are being undertaken by the country´s universities, research organizations, and government agencies like the DA and the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), to inform the public on how to handle this kind of science which is already in place not only abroad but also in the Philippines. He said that it is unfortunate that he was not given the opportunity to ask those questions and that the people were not enlightened on the subject. He however expressed hope that at the proper time, he would be given the chance to ask them.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 23,p.11)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOOD SECURITY since 2013-11-20

rows.author: F093;
rows.title_full: CONTINUING MILITARY PRESENCE IN MINING SITES AND HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AGAINST INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Defensor, the Chair recognized
Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan from Party-List
Gabriela who called the attention of the Body on the plight of indigenous women, more importantly to the continuing militarization and injustice that indigenous women are subjected to, as the country commemorates the Indigenous People´s Month and the International Rural Women´s Day.
She then narrated the case of a woman and her
children from the B´laan tribe who were killed during military operations as well as the human rights violations perpetuated against the Lumad or the indigenous people (IP) of Southern Mindanao, including the murder of an advocate and missionary for IP´s rights. Rep. Ilagan enjoined the Members to uphold the rights and interests of women in indigenous and rural
communities, to seek justice for IP victims of extrajudicial killings, to stop militarization in indigenous communities, and to protect ancestral lands from multinational mining companies and large-scale agricultural interests.
(SOURCE: Journal No. 23, p.11-12)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2013-11-20
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Atienza, Dela Cruz and Erice. Referred to the appropriate Committee. on Oct.22, 2013.

rows.author: A007;
rows.abstract:
Rep. Apostol delved on the issue of smuggling
besetting the Bureau of Customs (BOC), specifically that of the multibillion peso resin importation business, the massive technical smuggling of highend and expensive motor vehicles, oil smuggling, and rice smuggling. He said that he has the pertinent information to support his allegations, which he would present to the House in case of a committee investigation thereon. He then urged the Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability to immediately conduct a thorough investigation of smuggling activities in the Bureau and summon all BOC officials and personnel involved as well as representatives of different business groups to shed light on the issues of corruption and smuggling.
(SOURCE: Journal No.24,pp.7-8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2013-10-22
