rows.author: G101;
rows.title_full: DEVASTATION BROUGHT ABOUT BY THE EARTHQUAKE IN BOHOL
rows.abstract:
...Rep. Arthur C. Yap related how the recent earthquake that devastated his province had resulted in deaths, billion-worth of damage to
properties, and psychological trauma to almost 80% of the populace. He added that the calamity, which extended up to the Central Visayas, did not spare the nation´s cultural treasures that were constructed during the Spanish era and were all considered as national historical landmarks.
He thereafter thanked the Filipino people for
sharing their time, prayers and resources in helping the Boholanos, with no less than the President himself and some Cabinet Secretaries tending to the needs of the victims, and assured that they would all rise to the challenges before them. He said that he filed a measure establishing the Bakod Central Visayas that would appropriate funds for the relief and rehabilitation of Bohol and its people, and
further explained its goals and mechanisms.
He then asked the Members to immediately pass
the proposed budget Bill in order to help the poor victims of the affected provinces.
(SOURCE: Journal No.24,pp.16-17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-11-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: E001;
rows.title_full: REACTION TO A NEWSPAPER ARTICLE THAT MALIGNED HER FAMILY
rows.title_short: In Defense Of Batanes And Secretary Abad
rows.abstract:
Rep. Abad rose to respond to allegations
regarding the alleged involvement of several
government officials, especially her family, in the PDAF scam as well as the release of the Commission on Audit´s (COA) special report on PDAF utilization from 2007 to 2009. She conveyed her regret that the allegations of graft and fund misuse are again casting a shadow over the integrity of various government agencies, more so of the House of Representatives. Stressing the need for reform and greater transparency, Rep. Abad emphasized the importance of engaging the Filipino citizens in meaningful dialogues and making them active partners in order to accomplish those goals. She refuted the accusations blaming the Abad family on the pork barrel issue which were reported in an article that appeared in the Philippine Daily
Inquirer the basis of which, she said, were solely on the statements made by Buhay Party-List Rep. Jose L. Atienza Jr. She also underscored the development programs and projects that the Abad family has accomplished and would still do for the province of Batanes.
Rep. Abad emphasized that her family has
always maintained strict professionalism and
integrity and has always been resolute and
determined agents of profound change despite the
continuous attempts to malign them. She averred that the Filipino people are the ones suffering as they yearn for genuine change and call for sovereignty. She expressed optimism that in the end, with God´s help and the people´s inspiration, truth and honesty would prevail as her family continues to be steadfast in being good and honest public servants.
(SOURCE: Journal No.24,p.17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2013-11-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: G095;
rows.title_full: \"DESPOTIC\" ATTITUDE OF THE SUPREME COURT IN RENDERING THE DECISION ON THE PDAF
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Umali rose
in defense of a colleague; the House of
Representatives´ Electoral Tribunal (HRET); and the Philippine Constitution. Rep. Umali enumerated instances in defense of the Constitution, against judicial despots involving
the Supreme Court and its members who callously
disregard long established principles of law and
jurisprudence, in complete disrespect for the separate and independent powers of coequal branches of government through flip-flopping decisions. He then cited the high Court´s final
disqualification of Rep. Regina Ongsiako Reyes as a Member representing the Lone District of
Marinduque. He discussed the hasty dismissal of
Rep. Reyes´ petition for certiorari notwithstanding her proclamation by the Commission on Elections (Comelec); the view that the HRET should have decided on the case; the allegations of vested interests in the disqualification; and the constitutional
dilemma and legal absurdities arising from the
decision. In conclusion, Rep. Umali said that the judiciary should not be allowed to violate principles of law and jurisprudence and democratic doctrines or to emasculate the powers of Congress and the Executive. Impeachment complaints could be filed against it if does not rid itself of despots, he stressed.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. LOBREGAT
Rep. Umali agreed with Rep. Lobregat that the
recent Supreme Court decision on the PDAF was a
man-made calamity which affected the country more
strongly than the recent typhoons and earthquakes. Both Members then discussed the flip-flopping decisions and rulings of the Supreme Court particularly declaring previously the Countrywide Development Fund (CDF) and the PDAF as constitutional and now overturning its own ruling when it declared the PDAF and other lump-sum appropriations as unconstitutional. Rep. Lobregat stressed that the decision of the Supreme Court declaring the PDAF as unconstitutional rendered the legislators as helpless considering that their constituents expect them to bring projects and development to their districts. For his part, Rep. Umali urged his colleagues to fight for the powers and the mandate of Congress and take action, through the power of impeachment, against certain magistrates of the Supreme Court who are accountable for betrayal of public trust and
violate the principle of separation of powers.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. RIDON
Rep. Ridon discussed with Rep. Umali the
despotism of the Supreme Court particularly the
discretionary use of its funding known as the
Judiciary Development Fund (JDF). The latter stated that the Supreme Court spoke with unclean hands with regard to accountability and responsibility in the use of public funds, pointing out that the Supreme Court too has its own pork barrel system in the form of the JDF which the Chief Justice solely administers. They agreed that the fund should also be declared as unconstitutional and that Congress, through its oversight functions, should look into the
matter of the JDF which can be repealed as it was
created by a presidential decree.
(SOURCE: Journal No.32,p.16)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2014-01-22
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Lobregat and Ridon. Referred to the Committee on Rules (J.34,p.10)

rows.author: F110;
rows.title_full: WRATH OF TYPHOON YOLANDA
rows.title_short: Personal Experience On The Wrath Of Yolanda
rows.abstract:
Rep. Montejo narrated what he and other
survivors of the supertyphoon Yolanda in the Visayas had went through on what they called a second lease on life. After citing a phone call made by Science and Technology Secretary Mario Montejo to warn them of the magnitude and strength of the typhoon, he provided a personal account of the initial days of the onslaught and aftermath of the supertyphoon. He enumerated the grave and harrowing physical conditions that his family and the people from Tacloban City had endured and experienced: the absence of immediate relief and help during the first
day in the aftermath of supertyphoon Yolanda; the
lack of adequate and coordinated emergency
response by national and local government officials to the overwhelming devastation, chaos, looting, and lawlessness; and the absence of relief and food supplies and medical assistance. He underscored that an immediate and
coordinated emergency disaster program and relief
efforts implemented by the national government
agencies, the military and law-enforcement
organizations, and sociocivic agencies and the
provision for air-transport helicopters, satellite communications phones, and food and medical supplies would have addressed the need for emergency and disaster relief. Rep. Montejo thereafter expressed his gratitude to certain national and local government officials,
including the Metro Manila Development Authority
and the Bureau of Fire Protection of the Department of the Interior and Local Government, international groups, and his party-list coalition for their active participation in the emergency relief operations for the Yolanda victims. He then enjoined the Members to help in rebuilding and ensuring the rehabilitation of Region VIII. In closing, he requested the Members to stand up in honor of the dead and the victims of supertyphoon Yolanda.
(SOURCE: Journal No.33,p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2014-01-20
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F057;

rows.abstract:

rows.author: H090;
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR ADOPTION OF MEASURES TO RESPOND TO THE PLIGHT OF TYPHOON YOLANDA VICTIMS
rows.abstract:
Initially, Rep. Noel described the suffering of the victims of Typhoon Yolanda in Tacloban City in particular and in Region VIII in general. Subsequently, she acknowledged the foreign aid as well as the support and assistance from the media, the Philippine Army, the Chief Executive and House Speaker, and from the public and private groups including the public elementary pupils who sent letters of comfort and one-peso donations and the local government executives
who offered new lives and jobs. On behalf of the victims, Rep. Noel then suggested that Congress consider resolutions on price control for food and construction supplies, tax breaks
for food manufacturers, and Philhealth coverage; and enact measures for the purchase of more helicopters and appropriate communication equipment, and the authorized use of private communication facilities for calamities and emergencies. She informed the Body that she was already preparing a bill for a moratorium
of loan amortizations and a resolution for lowcost housing loans with a one-year moratorium on loan payments.
(SOURCE: Journal No.25,p.34)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee(Nov.20,2013)

rows.author: F061;
rows.title_full: EXPRESSED GRATITUDE TO THE NATION AND THE INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY FOR THE ASSISTANCE EXTENDED TO TYPHOON YOLANDA VICTIMS IN TACLOBAN CITY
rows.title_short: Devastation Caused By Typhoon Yolanda And The Different Measures To Be Taken After The Typhoon
rows.abstract:
Next recognized by the Chair, Rep. Ferdinand
Martin G. Romualdez also thanked the local and international community of nations for their relief and rehabilitation efforts as he showed a video presentation of death, injury, damage, and destruction as a result of the recent typhoon.
Rep. Romualdez stated that in response to the
widespread destruction and upon his request, together with the members of the independent Minority bloc, President Benigno S. Aquino III signed Proclamation No. 682 declaring the country in a state of national calamity. He then thanked the local and foreign media for bringing the plight of the typhoon victims to the attention of the whole world, as well as
the government institutions and nongovernment organizations (NGOs) both here and abroad for their financial contributions and relief and rehabilitation efforts. As he stressed that the Philippine government should also assume its responsibility in the rebuilding process, he called on his colleagues to consider the
following: 1) adoption of House Resolution No. 467 authorizing the use of P30 billion from the unspent portion of the P268 billion Special Purpose Fund for the relief, rehabilitation, and reconstruction of areas affected by natural calamities in accordance with the procedure and distribution system of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC); 2) approval of House Bill No. 3361, creating the Typhoon Yolanda Assistance and Development
Commission; 3) enactment of a tax break
measure for entrepreneurs that would want to establish their businesses in calamity-stricken areas; and 4) creation of a new government agency that will handle all calamity-related operations. Furthermore, Rep. Romualdez enjoined his colleagues to make a comprehensive study of the Local Government Code of 1991 in order to keep pace with the current situation particularly in strengthening the local government units (LGUs) in handling all kinds
of disasters and calamities. In closing and in behalf of the people of the Province of Leyte, Rep. Romualdez expressed his sincere gratitude to all those who have in one way or another helped them in their hour of need.
(SOURCE: Journal No.25,pp.34-35)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Atienza. Referred to the appropriate Committee(Nov.20,2013)

rows.author: G042;
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE CREATION OF THE VISAYAS COMMISSION FOR THE REHABILITATION OF AREAS ADVERSELY AFFECTED BY TYPHOON YOLANDA
rows.title_short: Master Plan For The Rehabilitation Of The Areas Affected By Typhoon Yolanda
rows.abstract:
On motion of Rep. Lagdameo (M.), the Chair
recognized Rep. Evardone who spoke about the steps that have to be taken to start rebuilding the communities ravaged by Yolanda, which included, among others, the creation of a Visayas Commission and the reconstitution of the 2014 national budget to form a money pool that would be dedicated for the rebuilding and reconstruction work in the affected Visayan
provinces. He also took note of the Body´s impending approval of Speaker Belmonte´s three proposals, to wit: creation of a P20-billion reconstruction fund, realignment of the 2013 Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) to the calamity fund, and request for each Member to contribute P10,000 to the relief fund.
Among other additional suggestions, Rep.Evardone proposed for a productive use by the country's economic managers of the substantial international aid pouring into the country in the form of monetary grants, loans, and investments that will accrue to the affected provinces. He also underscored the need for special health programs, housing and resettlement, employment opportunities, livelihood and financing programs for the typhoon victims. In closing, he expressed his gratitude to the Members of Congress who had provided prayers, assistance and show of support to the victims of Typhoon Yolanda. Thereupon, the Chair recognized Rep. Karlo Alexei B. Nograles for his interpellation.
INTERPELLATION OF REP. NOGRALES
Reps. Nograles and Evardone´s discussion centered
on the important lessons to be drawn from the
United States´ (US) experience with Hurricane
Katrina in 2005 which could have been applied in the case of the Philippines in the wake of Typhoon Yolanda, as well as on the funds needed to adequately and properly rehabilitate and reconstruct the typhoon-devastated areas.
Even as the LGUs in his province had made the
necessary preparations before the super typhoon
made its landfall in the province, Rep. Evardone said that the sheer magnitude of the typhoon overpowered all their preemptive efforts. He agreed with Rep. Romualdez on the need to reassess the country´s disaster-preparedness programs and relevant protocols and laws. He however explained that an accurate estimate
of the needed rehabilitation fund could not be
determined at this time, considering the extent and enormity of the devastation to lives, properties, agricultural resources and infrastructures. Rep. Evardone agreed with Rep. Nograles´ remarks saying that any effort by the House would be very much appreciated, be it by way of enacting a supplemental budget, revising the current proposed budget for 2014, or any other means that would help rebuild and reconstitute the devastated communities.
Likewise, he agreed that the Members should study
the 600-page report by an American bipartisan committee that was created after Hurricane Katrina struck, and learn from America´s experience.
(SOURCE: Journal No.25,p.35-36)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Nograles. Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: F103;
rows.title_full: SUSTAINABLE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SECURITY AND CLIMATE CHANGE
rows.abstract:
Rep. Guanlao rose to discuss the damage brought
by Typhoon Yolanda to the agriculture sector
especially in the areas of food security and
sustainable food system. Adverting to a joint meeting held that morning by the Special Committee on Food Security and the Committee on Agriculture and Food to assess the food security situation in the country, he described a looming rice crisis considering that the National Food Authority (NFA) has reported a deficit in the rice reserve of the country. He mentioned that
the two Committees have recommended that the
targeting of rice reserve must factor in the probability of typhoons and that there must be a zero-tariff rate on rice importations during crisis situations. As he noted that the country is not alien to typhoons and the damages they cause to agriculture particularly in rice farming, Rep. Guanlao opined that the devastation caused by Typhoon Yolanda is
resonant to the call of the World Food Summit 2013 towards sustainable food systems, food security and nutrition.To attain these, he proposed among others, to: 1) increase productivity and productive capacities in the country´s food resource base; 2) re-nationalize
agricultural extension service structure and to amend the Local Government Code; 3) implement to the letter the provisions of the Farm Mechanization Act; 4) ensure the safe and affordable application of biotechnology;
5) review the land conversion policy in
agricultural lands and the Mining Act; and 6) employ adaptive production plans as well as modern technologies in weather forecasting, to enable agriculture to adapt to the exigencies of climate change. He then called on his colleagues to adopt House Resolution No. 124, creating the House Committee on Climate Change that would focus on the formulation of policies on climate change mitigation, adaptation and development; informed the Body that together with the other Members of the 16th Congress, he founded the Philippine chapter of a climate change parliament named Global International; and asked his colleagues to support House Bill No. 3180 which he authored, providing for the proper and adequate labeling of food.
(SOURCE: Journal No.26,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOOD SECURITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to appropriate Committee.

rows.author: D011;
rows.title_full: CHINESE INTRUSION INTO PHILIPPINE TERRITORY
rows.title_short: Mining Operations Of Chinese In The Country
rows.abstract:
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Fredenil
“Fred” H. Castro emphasized that the Province of
Capiz was also badly hit by Typhoon Yolanda but
that he had resisted from delivering a speech thereon pending the completion of an accurate situational report on the issue. He said that instead, he would focus on the issue of pork barrel that has caught the imagination and varied reactions of the Filipino people and which has resulted in the evolution of a
public opinion, the most illustrative of which was the million-people march initially held in Luneta Park on August 26, 2013 demanding for the abolition of the pork barrel from the 2014 national budget. Rep. Castro further talked about the creeping Chinese invasion of the mainland Philippines, which he opined should be given the highest priority by the national government. He cited excerpts from a news
story penned by Jarius Bondoc, exposing destructive small mines as well as illegal mining in Zambales, Cagayan and Leyte. He claimed that the small mines set up through Filipino dummies are allegedly just fronts of giant nickel miners from China and that the
nickel mines have aggravated air and sea pollution in many towns. Rep. Castro appealed to all Departments concerned and their attached agencies whether singly or in collaboration with each other, to investigate and initiate appropriate criminal action, including the
arrest and detention of all pillagers who arrogantly violate the Constitution and laws of the nation on the development and exploitation of its natural resources as well as those who violate the Anti-Dummy Law and other related laws. After positively identifying these pillagers, he then called for their immediate investigation, arrest and detention including their Filipino collaborators and recommended that repair on the damaged areas of the country´s natural resources be undertaken at
the expense of the alleged pillagers. Lastly, he
thanked columnist Jarius Bondoc for his noble deed.
(SOURCE: Journal No.26,p.7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2014-01-21
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H065;
rows.title_full: SUPREME COURT DECISION ON THE P D A F
rows.title_short: Unconstitutionality Of Priority Development Assistance Fund ( P D A F )
rows.abstract:
Rep. Atienza congratulated the Supreme Court
for its decision with a vote of 14-0, declaring all Congressional Pork Barrel Laws, such as the Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) and the Countrywide Development Fund (CDF), as illegal and unconstitutional. He said that this strengthens the roots of democracy in the country and inspires Members of Congress to adhere to the rule of law and the Constitution, and redirects their focus on crafting better legislations. He claimed that the Members must heed the decision and defer seeking alternatives
to obtain public funds for political patronage and personal interest. He further underscored the decision of the Supreme Court as a historic event to the Filipino people, to Philippine democracy, and to governance inasmuch as Members of Congress will no longer be made beholden to pork barrel funds and be subjected to the control and restraint of the Executive Department. He explained that the decision of the Supreme Court however provides a colatilla that those responsible for the misuse of public funds will be made accountable. In closing, Rep. Atienza stated that the decision of the Supreme Court declaring the PDAF illegal and unconstitutional should compel the Members of Congress to set aside partisanship, eradicate vestiges of personal interest, and exert utmost efforts for change in the government and political system in accordance with the hopes of the Filipino people.
(SOURCE: Journal No.26,p.8)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: H044;
rows.title_full: NEED TO STRENGTHEN THE RURAL IMPROVEMENT CLUB OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: R I C's Lack Of Funding Fro The Government
rows.abstract:
Rep. Macrohon-Nuño lamented the lack of funding
and technical support from the Department of
Agriculture (DA) for rural improvement clubs (RICs) in the country. She said these were nonprofit, nonsectarian and nonpartisan sociocivic organizations of rural women to improve their economic condition through agricultural skills training, foster mutual cooperation and camaraderie, and ensure a dynamic
partnership between the government and womenfolk
through livelihood projects. She thereafter cited statistics on the RICs´ membership by region; traced their history; and stressed that they were potent tools to improve the economic life of the countryside and as support to government efforts in building a strong and vibrant Republic. She emphasized the absence of a specific budget allocation for the RICs in the proposed 2014 DA budget and raised her concern on the monitoring of fund release, financial reports by the recipients of funds and the exercise of legislative oversight by the House to improve the activities of rural-based organizations. In closing, she encouraged her colleagues to support the RICs in their respective districts.
(HOUSE: Journal No.27,p.5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on RURAL DEVELOPMENT since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Referred to the appropriate Committee.

rows.author: C009;
rows.title_full: IMPROVING THE DISASTER RISK REDUCTION AND MANAGEMENT MEASURES OF THE GOVERNMENT
rows.abstract:
On behalf of the people of Isabela, Rep. Albano
offered sympathy to the people of Eastern and Western Visayas, particularly the provinces of Leyte and Samar which bore the brunt of Typhoon Yolanda. Coming from a province that had also been the victim of countless typhoons, he also offered thoughts and insights on how to deal with future calamities and natural resources.
As he noted the problem of distribution and delivery of food and medicines to the worst-hit areas, he suggested the immediate clearing of roads and bridges to allow the easy transport of emergency goods. He also focused on the preparedness and capacity of the engineering construction brigades of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) under the Department of National Defense (DND) and the district
engineering teams of the Department of Public
Works and Highways (DPWH), and the need to realign the proposed budget of the military to fully perform its task in times of disasters or calamities, or even in the absence thereof, to address its mandate of nation-building rather than preparing for war. He also suggested the review and amendment of the Civil Defense Act under Republic Act (RA) No. 1190 to assess its relevance when threats come not from the Cold War but from global warming. This as he emphasized the need for the DND to map out appropriate plans and strategies for disaster prevention, preparedness, response and rehabilitation. Rep. Albano then asked for unity in this critical period and support for relief, recovery and rehabilitation efforts in the typhoon-ravaged areas. He also affirmed that the government should learn from this tragedy and turn it into an opportunity to improve its
disaster-preparedness, response and prevention
measures.
(SOURCE: Journal No.27,p.6-7)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2013-12-03
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Biazon, Dela Cruz, Seneres, Loong and Farinas. Referred to the appropriate Committee.
